title: Software Engineer, Data Flywheel Platform
description:
About Wayve and the team

Wayve is building embodied AI for the physical world, starting with autonomous driving. Instead of the hand-engineered, modular stacks that defined the first era of self-driving, we pioneered AV2.0: a single, end-to-end neural network that learns to drive from raw sensor data and generalizes to new cities, vehicles, and conditions. Our foundation models, the GAIA family of generative world models and the LINGO family of vision-language-action models, allow vehicles to perceive, reason, and act in the open world. We have driven zero-shot across hundreds of cities on three continents, and we are now scaling from proving the science to deploying it with leading automakers and mobility partners, including Nissan, Stellantis, and Uber.

This role sits in the AI Platform organization, on the data flywheel that powers every model we ship. Applied Scientists and ML Engineers on the team push the frontier on data curation, enrichment, foundation-model evaluation, and the models themselves. This role builds the platform underneath all of it: the pipelines, infrastructure, and systems that turn world-scale fleet data into high-signal training data, evaluate and train foundation models, and enable every team to run these workflows themselves. As deployment scales, the leverage is enormous: the better the platform, the faster the whole flywheel turns.

The role

We are hiring a senior Software Engineer to build the platform that powers Wayve’s data flywheel and foundation-model stack. This is the engineering counterpart to our Applied Scientist and ML Engineer roles: you build the systems they, and the wider company, depend on. It is high-leverage, high-visibility work with a clear path to deep system ownership.

  • Build the systems that allow teams to turn world-scale driving data into high-signal training data, and evaluate and train foundation models on it.

  • Replace ad-hoc scripts and manual handoffs with self-serve, observable products used across Science, Autonomy, and Evaluation.

  • Every model Wayve ships runs on this platform: your work compounds across the entire fleet and roadmap.

  • Work shoulder to shoulder with a world-class science and engineering team, with real deployment at global OEM scale (Nissan, Stellantis, Uber).

  • TC3 / TC4 ownership of platform and infrastructure, with room to set technical direction as the platform matures.

What you will do

  • Build and scale the data curation and enrichment pipelines that turn world-scale fleet data into high-signal training data: mining and active-learning loops, running model-based enrichments over billions of rows, and ensuring data quality at scale.

  • Build the evaluation infrastructure behind foundation-model progress: harnesses for offline and closed-loop evaluation, metric and benchmark pipelines, and world-model-based evaluation.

  • Build and optimize training and serving infrastructure for large pretrained models: distributed training, batched inference, and large-scale model backfills.

  • Build the data-platform backbone: distributed data processing (Ray Data, Daft, Spark / Databricks), embedding and vector search (turbopuffer, Milvus), lakehouse formats (Lance, Iceberg), dataset versioning, and the enrichment and annotation catalog.

  • Make it self-serve and reliable: turn one-off processes into products that other teams operate themselves, and own testing, observability, and on-call for what you ship.

  • Partner closely with Applied Scientists and ML Engineers to take research from prototype to production at scale.

What we are looking for

  • Strong production software engineering, especially production Python (services, APIs, large-scale data processing), and comfort owning and extending large codebases.

  • Large-scale data and distributed-systems experience: batch and streaming pipelines, workflow orchestration (Flyte, Airflow, Dagster, or similar), and distributed processing (Spark / PySpark, Ray, Databricks, or equivalent).

  • Systems design for scale: reliable, observable, high-throughput data or ML systems, with strong SQL and query and performance optimization.

  • A track record of shipping and operating production systems that other teams depend on: testing, code review, observability, and on-call.

  • Strong CS fundamentals and several years of production experience (roughly 6 or more for TC3, more for TC4), or equivalent; a degree in CS or comparable practical experience.

  • Seniority to match the level: takes ambiguous, cross-team problems and drives them to completion, and at TC4 sets technical direction and multiplies the team.

Bonus points

  • ML platform / MLOps: model registration, distributed training, and inference or serving optimization.

  • Enough exposure to foundation models, world models, or ML evaluation to partner deeply with scientists.

  • Embedding and vector search, annotation tooling, or feature and data catalogs.

  • Kubernetes and modern data / lakehouse stacks (Databricks, Lance, Iceberg).

  • Autonomous driving, robotics, or other large-scale sensor-data workflows.

About Us

Spellman High Voltage Electronics Corporation, a family owned business for over 75 years, takes pride in powering progress in health, security and quality of life. · Review detailed fabrication and assembly drawings for accuracy and tolerances

· Determine parts, equipment, and tools needed to achieve manufacturing goals according to product specifications

· Design tooling and fixturing for production and quality control

· Develop and optimize process flow and work instructions

· Support low-volume production to verify achievement of process plans and targets for quality, safety, efficiency, and cost.

· Experience with AutoCAD, Inventor, Solid Works, and/or other types of CAD or 3D modeling software

· Gerber/PCB software (viewers)

· Microsoft Office

· Minimum 3 years of electronics manufacturing experience.

· Understanding of ISO, IPC, and J-Standard

· Ability to read and understand electrical schematics and assembly drawings

· Strong written and verbal skills.

· Team leadership ability and exceptional organizational skills.

title: Full Stack Engineer
description:
Software Engineer, AI & Data Platform (Python/Go)

Vancouver, BC · Remote (Canada)

Why this role is interesting

Most engineers building with LLMs right now are building chat interfaces. You'd be building something harder.

OneMedNet supplies regulatory-grade Real World Data and imaging Real World Data to life sciences, pharma, and medical device researchers. That means clinical records and medical imaging studies that have to be de-identified, curated, and validated to a standard that holds up under FDA scrutiny — at scale, across a growing network of hospital and clinic partners.

The interesting problems live in that gap: how do you use language models to accelerate curation of messy, high-stakes clinical data without ever compromising accuracy or patient privacy? How do you build inference pipelines that are auditable enough for a regulated environment? How do you make complex cohort data legible to a researcher in a browser?

That's the work.

What you'll do

  • Build LLM-powered features for clinical data curation and retrieval — prompt design, evaluation, API integration, and the pipelines that hold it all together
  • Design and ship backend services in Python and/or Go that move structured records, unstructured clinical notes, DICOM imaging, and HL7/FHIR messaging securely and fast
  • Answer questions that close deals. When Sales is scoping a contract, someone has to query partner systems and determine what data actually exists and in what volume. That's engineering work, and it directly determines whether a deal happens
  • Build the interfaces researchers actually use to search, filter, and visualize cohorts
  • Own quality end to end: instrument your LLM features, monitor for drift and regression, and know when a model output is good enough to ship
  • Work directly with the clinical and data teams who define what "regulatory grade" means for a given dataset

What we need from you

  • 2+ years shipping production software with strong Python and/or Go
  • Real experience building on LLM APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, or similar) — you've shipped something that used one, and you've dealt with the failure modes
  • Comfort across the stack. You don't need to be a design specialist, but you can build a functional, clear interface without waiting on someone else
  • Strong SQL and database fundamentals — schema design, query performance, and knowing when relational is the wrong answer
  • Working comfort in AWS and Linux. Our platform runs on AWS (S3, EC2, RDS, VPC, IAM) in Ubuntu environments. You should be able to operate there without hand-holding
  • Judgment about correctness. In healthcare data, a plausible-but-wrong answer is worse than no answer. We need engineers who feel that in their bones

Our stack

Python and Go. AWS (S3, EC2, RDS, VPC, IAM) on Ubuntu Linux. Snowflake and Palantir for data and AI workloads. Anthropic and OpenAI APIs. Postgres. Git-based workflows.

Nice to have

  • Healthcare, clinical data, or medical imaging experience (DICOM, HL7/FHIR)
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA, GDPR, or technical de-identification techniques for PHI/PII
  • Snowflake or Palantir experience
  • Experience with model evaluation frameworks or LLM observability tooling
  • Data visualization work

We'll teach you the healthcare part.

Compensation & benefits

  • $80,000 – $120,000 CAD depending on experience, plus performance bonus
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Flexible schedule and fully remote across Canada
  • A small team at a real inflection point in an emerging market

OneMedNet is committed to privacy and compliance, meeting or exceeding HIPAA, GDPR, and other applicable privacy standards to protect patient information.

title: Senior Geotechnical Engineer
description:
As a Senior Geotechnical Engineer, you will play a key role in delivering high-impact geotechnical and performance-based design projects. This role offers a unique opportunity to lead, mentor, and grow a team engaged in some of our most advanced analytical work. You’ll collaborate proactively with internal and external partners to develop innovative solutions to complex geotechnical challenges, contributing to the technical direction of the group.


A strong background in seismic design and earthquake engineering is essential. You’ll take ownership of key project activities, including developing conceptual and numerical models, managing project schedules, writing technical reports, supporting client relationships, coordinating subsurface exploration programs, and overseeing construction observation. Your leadership will help drive the group’s long-term technical development and elevate the sophistication of our performance-based design capabilities.


Typical projects span complex geotechnical applications, including liquefaction and seismic slope stability evaluations, ground improvement design, and dynamic nonlinear deformation analyses of temporary and permanent shored excavations in dense urban environments alongside a steady mix of conventional geotechnical engineering work. From foundations and retaining structures to earthwork, pavements, and construction-phase support, you’ll contribute across the full spectrum of our practice. While responsibilities vary by project, leadership, technical rigor, and collaborative problem-solving will remain at the core of your work. This role can be performed out of our Seattle, San Diego, or Redmond office.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Leads project management activities, including developing budgets and scopes, client billings, field report reviews, preparing proposals, contract reviews, and coordinating with Principals and Associates to ensure effective execution of multiple projects.
  • Serves as a senior technical resource in numerical modeling and nonlinear deformation analysis. Provides guidance to project teams and offers expertise on complex geotechnical and performance-based design challenges.
  • Develops advanced conceptual and numerical models, including dynamic and static analyses, liquefaction and lateral spreading evaluations, and soil-structure interaction assessments.
  • Reviews and oversees deliverables from staff and mid-level engineers, including calculations, analyses, and field reports, providing clear direction and feedback to support high-quality work.
  • Mentors and develops junior staff, offering leadership across technical skill-building, project execution, and consulting best practices.
  • Participates in business development, including identifying new opportunities, maintaining client relationships, and attending conferences or professional association meetings.
  • Leads or coordinates subsurface exploration programs and construction-phase activities, collaborating closely with contractors and field staff and maintaining alignment with project requirements and safety protocols.
  • Prepares high-quality technical documentation, including reports, figures, and tables that require minimal revision.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering required; Master’s degree or a PhD in Geotechnical Engineering preferred.
  • 6+ years of experience with dynamic numerical modeling or related professional experience required.
  • PE license required.
  • Strong proficiency with FLAC, PLAXIS, and related tools, including experience with dynamic soil-structure interaction and nonlinear deformation modeling.
  • Demonstrated ability to evaluate seismic hazards such as ground response, liquefaction, lateral spreading, and seismic slope instability.
  • Proven leadership, mentorship, and team-building skills.
  • Strong proactive responsiveness and the ability to meet tight deadlines in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.
  • Professional-level verbal and written communication skills.

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

  • All candidates are subject to completing a background check, and reference check.
  • Ability to perform a wide range of physical activities and do heavy work including exerting up to 50 pounds of force on occasion.
  • Ability to perform consistent work on a PC with prolonged sitting and view of a monitor/screen.
  • Ability to travel for short-term and long-term assignments as needed.
  • All employees are responsible for conducting their work in a safe manner. This includes identifying potential safety hazards and reporting them to the designated project manager in a timely manner and participating in project safety briefings. This also includes wearing appropriate safety equipment when working in the field and completing all required health & safety training prior to beginning fieldwork.

Our best estimate of the salary range for this position, located in Seattle, Redmond, WA, or San Diego, CA is $117,000 - $176,000 annually. Compensation offered will be based on a variety of individual factors, including education and experience, as well as internal equity. GeoEngineers’ salary ranges are reviewed and updated each year and employees are eligible for pay increases based on individual performance. As part of our competitive total rewards package, employees in this role may also be eligible for our annual year-end bonus offering, subject to program eligibility requirements.


At GeoEngineers, investing in our people is a top priority. In addition to competitive and equitable pay, we are proud to offer a wide range of benefits to support employees and their families, including healthcare (with travel benefit for care not locally available), 401(k) with company match, short-term and long-term disability, life insurance, wellbeing benefits, paid vacation and sick time and paid holidays, among others. title: Revenue Cycle Finance Liaison
description:
Position Overview

The Revenue Cycle Finance Liaison serves as the primary bridge between the Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) and Finance/Accounting teams. This role is responsible for ensuring revenue cycle-related financial activity is accurately recorded, reconciled, and reflected in the organization's financial reporting.

The Revenue Cycle Finance Liaison serves as the primary point of contact for finance-related RCM questions and works closely with billing, collections, cash posting, and accounting teams to investigate discrepancies, validate transactions, and improve the accuracy and integrity of revenue-related financial reporting.

The ideal candidate has a strong understanding of skilled nursing facility revenue cycle operations, payer reimbursement, cash posting, contractual adjustments, revenue adjustments, and accounts receivable reconciliation.


Duties:


· Serve as the primary liaison between Revenue Cycle Management and Finance/Accounting for revenue cycle-related financial matters.

· Serve as the first point of contact for finance-related RCM questions and ensure inquiries are researched and resolved accurately and timely.

· Review and reconcile non-AR cash transactions to ensure appropriate general ledger coding and accurate financial reporting.

· Review revenue adjustments to validate accuracy, appropriateness, and proper recording.

· Review payer payments, postings, and adjustments to ensure they align with contractual expectations and internal policies.

· Partner with Finance to investigate and resolve discrepancies involving cash, revenue, accounts receivable, and general ledger activity.

· Support month-end close by validating revenue-related transactions and completing required reconciliation activities.

· Complete the prior month's required revenue cycle financial review by the 10th of each month.

· Work closely with billing, collections, cash posting, and accounting teams to resolve financial discrepancies and improve processes.

· Analyze revenue cycle financial activity to identify errors, trends, and areas requiring further investigation.

· Identify and recommend process improvements related to revenue recognition, cash application, reconciliation, and financial reporting.

· Support internal and external audits by providing requested documentation and explanations related to revenue cycle financial activity.

· Maintain clear documentation of reconciliations, identified discrepancies, resolutions, and recurring issues.

· Escalate material discrepancies or unresolved issues to appropriate Revenue Cycle and Finance leadership.

· Meet deadlines and delivery commitments as agreed upon with management and proactively communicate risks or barriers that may impact timely completion.

· Perform other duties as assigned.


Competencies:


· Revenue Cycle Expertise: Strong understanding of healthcare revenue cycle processes, reimbursement, billing, collections, cash posting, and accounts receivable.

· Financial Reconciliation: Ability to reconcile financial activity, investigate discrepancies, and validate the accuracy of transactions.

· Analytical Thinking: Ability to analyze detailed financial and operational information, identify trends and inconsistencies, and determine appropriate next steps.

· Attention to Detail: Consistently demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness when reviewing financial transactions and supporting documentation.

· Problem Solving: Ability to identify root causes and work across departments to drive issues through resolution.

· Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to effectively bridge Revenue Cycle and Finance and build strong working relationships across teams.

· Accountability: Takes ownership of assigned reconciliations, inquiries, deadlines, and follow-up through completion.

· Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly explain financial and revenue cycle matters to operational and financial stakeholders.

description:
About the Role

This is a founding-stage role sitting at the core of a Berlin-based personalized healthtech company, working directly with the founders to ship ideas quickly and eliminate manual work through AI and automation. You'll help build repeatable, measurable systems that improve member outcomes in a regulated health context — with the possibility of converting to a full-time role after a 3–6 month engagement.

description:

Remote Position

Position Summary

The IT Systems Engineer (EUC) is responsible for the administration, support, and optimization of enterprise end-user computing, digital workspace, identity management, and Windows server technologies. As a Tier 2/Tier 3 escalation resource, this role ensures the security, reliability, and performance of Windows endpoints, virtual desktop infrastructure, identity platforms, and enterprise applications across a large, multi-site healthcare environment. Working closely with cross-functional IT teams, the Systems Engineer delivers scalable, secure solutions while supporting more than 5,000 users and endpoints.

Key Performance Areas

KPA 1 – Endpoint Engineering and Support

  • Provide Tier 2/Tier 3 support for Windows 10 and Windows 11 endpoint technologies.
  • Administer and support endpoint operating systems, configurations, policies, and application deployments.
  • Support endpoint lifecycle activities including deployment, upgrades, patching, and retirement.
  • Troubleshoot complex workstation, application, authentication, and performance issues.
  • Administer and support Group Policy Objects (GPOs), endpoint security controls, and configuration standards.
  • Support Microsoft 365 applications and services related to endpoint computing.
  • Collaborate with Service Desk teams to resolve escalated incidents and service requests.
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, knowledge articles, and operational procedures.

KPA 2 – Virtual Desktop Infrastructure and Application Delivery

  • Serve as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops, and virtual application delivery technologies.
  • Administer and support Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) environments.
  • Administer and support Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops environments.
  • Provide technical leadership and expert guidance for the design, implementation, troubleshooting, and optimization of virtual desktop and application delivery solutions.
  • Monitor and optimize virtual desktop performance, availability, and user experience.
  • Manage application publishing, desktop delivery, profile management, and user access.
  • Support FSLogix profile containers and Microsoft 365 integration within virtual environments.
  • Perform routine maintenance, upgrades, patching, and platform health assessments.
  • Participate in capacity planning, performance tuning, and scalability initiatives.
  • Develop and maintain technical standards, documentation, and best practices for virtual desktop infrastructure.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure, networking, security, and application teams to ensure the stability, security, and availability of the virtual workspace environment.
  • Provide Tier 3/escalation support and technical mentoring for complex virtual desktop and application delivery issues.
  • Support end-user access and application delivery across virtual workspace platforms.

KPA 3 – Identity and Access Management

  • Administer and support Okta Identity Management platform.
  • Administer and support Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory environments.
  • Support Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and Conditional Access policies.
  • Troubleshoot authentication, access, and identity synchronization issues.
  • Assist with user provisioning, deprovisioning, and access governance processes.
  • Administer Active Directory users, groups, organizational units, and Group Policy.
  • Partner with Security teams to support compliance and security initiatives.

KPA 4 – Clinical Workspace Technologies

  • Administer and support Imprivata authentication and clinical workflow solutions.
  • Administer and support IGEL endpoint and thin-client platforms.
  • Support shared workstation and clinical workstation environments.
  • Troubleshoot end-user access issues involving virtual desktops, authentication workflows, and endpoint devices.
  • Collaborate with Clinical Operations and application teams to optimize clinician workflows and user experience.
  • Participate in testing and deployment of new workspace technologies and enhancements.
  • Support healthcare-specific technologies and secure clinical access solutions.

KPA 5 – Windows Server Administration and Infrastructure Support

  • Provide Tier 2/Tier 3 support for physical and virtual Windows Server environments.
  • Support Windows Server 2016, 2019, and 2022 operating systems.
  • Perform server patching, upgrades, maintenance, and operational support activities.
  • Administer and support Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, file services, and print services.
  • Monitor server performance, availability, and operational health.
  • Troubleshoot server-related incidents and service disruptions.
  • Participate in disaster recovery testing and business continuity activities.
  • Collaborate with Infrastructure Engineering teams on server lifecycle management, maintenance, and technology upgrades.
  • Maintain server documentation, configuration standards, and operational procedures.

KPA 6 – Service Operations and Continuous Improvement

  • Manage assigned incidents, requests, problems, and project tasks through completion.
  • Follow established ITIL processes for Incident, Problem, Change, and Knowledge Management.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of configurations, procedures, support processes, and system inventories.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvement, automation, and operational efficiencies.
  • Coordinate with vendors and internal technology teams to resolve complex technical issues.
  • Participate in after-hours maintenance activities and on-call support as required.
  • Communicate system risks, outages, and service-impacting issues to IT leadership.
  • Assist with training and knowledge transfer to Service Desk and junior IT staff.

Position Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field preferred. Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.

Minimum Relevant Experience

  • Minimum of 8 years of experience supporting enterprise IT environments.
  • Experience supporting and managing enterprise environments with 5,000+ endpoints and users across multiple locations.
  • Experience supporting large-scale End User Computing (EUC) and Digital Workspace environments; healthcare or other highly regulated industry experience preferred.
  • Experience supporting Windows 10 and Windows 11 operating systems.
  • Experience administering Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) and Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops.
  • Experience administering Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, and Microsoft 365.
  • Experience supporting Windows Server 2016, 2019, and 2022 in both physical and virtual environments.
  • Experience supporting IGEL and Imprivata solutions preferred.
  • Experience working in healthcare and multi-site enterprise environments preferred.

description:

The Mission

Join a global Newsroom Transformation team working at the intersection of backend engineering, AI, and modern journalism technology. You’ll build scalable backend services while helping integrate AI capabilities into news systems, including LLM orchestration, fine-tuning, RAG, and intelligent automation.


You’ll collaborate with engineering teams and global stakeholders across multiple regions, helping transform how AI and automation power the next generation of newsroom platforms.


The Role

  • Model Strategy: Work with models such as Google Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic, selecting the right model based on performance, capabilities, and cost.

  • Python: Basic to intermediate Python experience for AI/ML development and model-related tasks.
  • LangChain: Hands-on experience with LangChain is mandatory.
  • AI / LLMs: Strong understanding of NLP, tokenization, embeddings, prompt engineering, LLM fine-tuning, and RAG architectures.
  • Cloud & DevOps: Experience with Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and at least one major cloud provider — Google Cloud preferred, AWS acceptable.
  • Microservices: Strong understanding of distributed and microservice architectures.
  • Global Collaboration: Comfortable working asynchronously across multiple time zones and collaborating with international stakeholders.


The "Bonus" Skills

  • Infrastructure as Code: Experience with Terraform.
  • Legacy Technologies: Familiarity with PHP.
  • Media & Publishing: Experience working in media, publishing, journalism, or newsroom technology.
  • GTM Experience: Exposure to startup environments and Go-to-Market strategies.
  • Advanced MLOps: Experience with model evaluation, validation, monitoring, and production AI/ML pipelines.


Personal Traits

  • AI-Minded Engineer: Excited about applying LLMs and emerging AI technologies to real-world products and workflows.
  • Backend Problem Solver: Enjoys building reliable, scalable services and solving complex distributed-system challenges.
  • Pragmatic Technologist: Able to evaluate models, tools, and approaches based on technical requirements, quality, and cost.
  • Strong Communicator: Comfortable presenting ideas, explaining technical decisions, and working with stakeholders across different regions.
  • Self-Driven: Thrives in a remote, asynchronous environment and takes initiative without constant direction.
  • Global Collaborator: Enjoys working across cultures, time zones, and engineering teams to deliver high-impact solutions.

title: Business Data Analyst
description:
Job Description

Business Data Analyst

RONIN - Australia (Remote)

Not another BA brief. Read this one properly.

Business Data Analyst

Somewhere inside a well-established Australian organisation, a multi-year data transformation programme is quietly reshaping how the business understands itself. They need an intermediate-level Business Data Analyst (Business Intelligence) who can sit between the people who ask for reports and the people who build them, and translate one into the other without losing anything in the middle.

This is deliberately not a lead or principal-level position, and it's not rated as one. If you're used to running the show end-to-end with a team under you, this will feel like a step down, not a lateral move. If you're a few years in, sharp, hands-on, and happy to be part of a delivery team rather than running it, keep reading.

What you'll actually be doing

  • Sitting in workshops and interviews, asking the annoying-but-necessary questions nobody else thinks to ask
  • Turning business waffle into functional requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria that a delivery team can actually build from
  • Working elbow-to-elbow with BI and Data Engineering to keep requirements grounded in reality
  • Running traceability between what was asked for, what was built, and what was tested (so nothing quietly disappears along the way)
  • Supporting UAT, defect triage, and the odd stakeholder demo where you get to show off the finished product

What you'll bring

  • Circa 3+ years turning business needs into clear, documented requirements (this is an intermediate role, priced and scoped accordingly, so if you're operating at senior/lead/principal level with the day rate to match, this one won't be a fit)
  • Comfortable enough with SQL and relational data concepts to hold your own in a technical conversation
  • Some exposure to conceptual/logical data modelling (bonus, not a dealbreaker)
  • Agile or hybrid delivery experience
  • The diplomacy to manage a room full of senior stakeholders with competing opinions, without losing the plot

The practical bits

  • Contract role, intermediate level, rate set accordingly
  • Remote friendly
  • No direct reports of your own to manage (just requirements)

If this sounds like your kind of chaos, and the level's right for you, get in touch.

description:
Want to apply data science to one of Amazon's fastest-growing payment businesses, serving millions of sellers and buyers across 20+ global marketplaces? As a Data Scientist I on the cross-border payments science team, you will build and deploy production models that power real-time FX risk monitoring, generative AI seller chatbots, and multi-agent AI tools. You will work end-to-end—from problem framing through production deployment on AWS—delivering solutions that directly influence billion-dollar payment flows. This is a high-visibility, small-team environment where your work informs senior leadership decisions and creates measurable impact for customers worldwide.

Key job responsibilities
- Build, tune, and evaluate large language models and generative AI applications, including seller-facing chatbots and multi-agent AI tools for the cross-border payments business.
- Develop and deploy real-time statistical and machine learning models for FX risk monitoring, validating your data, assumptions, and results throughout the process.
- Gather and use large datasets from multiple sources across global marketplaces to design production-ready solutions that meet customer needs and team goals.
- Write accurate, clear, and mathematically rigorous technical documents that communicate model performance and business impact to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Partner with engineering, business, and science teams to translate payment-domain problems into data science solutions and ensure smooth deployment on AWS.

A day in the life
You will spend your morning reviewing model outputs from production FX risk systems and tuning generative AI prototypes for seller chatbots. In the afternoon you might pair with an engineer to deploy a new model version on AWS, then present preliminary results to senior leadership. Throughout, you will seek feedback from senior scientists on your methodology and collaborate with cross-functional partners to refine problem framing.

About the team
We are the science team behind Amazon's cross-border payments business, supporting products that serve millions of sellers and buyers across 20+ global marketplaces. Our team is small and at an inflection point—we are expanding our generative AI capabilities, building multi-agent systems, and strengthening real-time risk models. You will join a group that values end-to-end ownership, from research to production, and whose work directly shapes decisions on large-scale payment flows.

title: Senior Charging Systems Engineer
description:
We are seeking an engineer to lead the systems engineering, software integration and technical delivery of DC fast charging capability across Allye's energy storage products. Its central challenge is the delivery of a product that performs safely and predictably across a large population of electric vehicles and off highway machinery. Interoperability, validation and disciplined systems thinking is required, supported by substantial hands on software capability and sufficient depth in high voltage hardware to specify, direct and challenge suppliers.

Responsibilities

Systems architecture and requirements

  • Own the architecture of the charging system, from the DC bus and power conversion interface through to the vehicle coupler, including the control and communications architecture across it.
  • Define the requirements and interface specifications that internal engineering teams and external suppliers work to.
  • Define and document the operating envelope of the product, including supported vehicle populations, power levels, operating sequences and handled failure modes.
  • Lead build, buy and partner decisions on charge controllers, protocol stacks and test equipment, and hold suppliers to the specification.

Software and communications integration

  • Lead software integration for charging, working hands on and in conjunction with the embedded controls and application software teams.
  • Implement, integrate and debug the charging communication stack, including the digital communication protocols governing DC charging sessions and the legacy protocols still present in the vehicle population.
  • Own the control layer that maps a charging session onto the battery management and energy management systems, including power ramping, derating, thermal limits and state of charge policy.
  • Implement remote management and monitoring interfaces to industry protocol, and the supporting communication interfaces for session management and diagnostics.
  • Develop tooling and automation for test execution, log capture and fault analysis.

Interoperability, test and validation

  • Own the interoperability strategy for the product, including the definition and maintenance of the supported vehicle matrix and the evidence base behind it.
  • Specify, procure and operate the charging test and validation capability, including vehicle and charger simulation and hardware in the loop testing.
  • Plan and lead structured interoperability campaigns, including participation in recognised industry test events, and convert the results into a managed defect and improvement backlog.
  • Diagnose faults at protocol and physical layer, including communication link establishment, insulation and cable verification, precharge and contactor sequencing, timeout and retry behaviour, and manufacturer specific deviations from standard.
  • Own the field return and failure investigation process for charging, including on site diagnosis, reproduction, resolution and verification.

High voltage interface and safety

  • Specify the physical charging interface, including couplers, cables, cooling strategy, cable management, ingress and impact protection, locking and temperature monitoring.
  • Define the DC side protection and isolation strategy, including switching and protective devices, insulation and residual current monitoring, earthing and protective conductor continuity, and touch safety.
  • Own the safety case for DC charging, including hazard analysis, failure mode and effects analysis, and shutdown and emergency stop behaviour.
  • Work with mechanical engineering on physical integration, cable routing, thermal management and enclosure design.

Standards, compliance and certification

  • Ensure the product conforms to the relevant international and national standards for DC charging, electrical safety, electromagnetic compatibility and functional safety applicable in the UK and European markets.
  • Support product conformity assessment and marking, and manage the technical relationship with test houses, certification bodies and notified bodies.
  • Maintain a current view of the evolution of the charging standards and of emerging requirements such as automated authorisation and bidirectional operation, and advise on their implications for the product roadmap.

Collaboration and technical leadership

  • Act as Allye's technical authority on charging, providing direction and guidance to engineering colleagues and to external partners, suppliers and customers.
  • Produce and maintain the technical documentation set, including specifications, integration guidance, test evidence and service and troubleshooting material.
  • Support commercial, product and field teams with technical input to customer requirements, deployment and after sales.

Essential knowledge and experience

  • Degree in electrical, electronic, control, software or systems engineering, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Five to eight years of relevant engineering experience, including a period of demonstrable technical ownership.
  • Direct experience of DC charging systems, on either the vehicle or the charging equipment side, taken through to production and operated with third party equipment.
  • Demonstrable experience of resolving interoperability faults between independently developed systems, personally and at the level of the protocol.
  • Practical competence in the design, integration and safe operation of high voltage DC systems.

Essential technical skills

  • Working knowledge of the DC charging standards and the associated communication protocols, and of the coupler and connector standards.
  • Proficiency in embedded software development in C or C++, and in a scripting language such as Python for tooling, automation and analysis.
  • Competence with industrial and automotive communication protocols and with IP networking, and with the associated diagnostic and analysis tooling.
  • Structured approach to requirements, verification and test, with the ability to produce evidence rather than assertion.
  • Version control, code review and collaborative software development practice.

Essential behaviours

  • Systems thinking. The ability to hold electrical, software, mechanical and regulatory considerations in view simultaneously and to make defensible trade offs between them.
  • Technical authority combined with accessibility. The capacity to be the organisation's expert in a specialist domain and to explain it clearly to colleagues who are not.
  • Autonomy and ownership. Comfortable operating with limited precedent and taking responsibility for outcomes rather than activity.
  • Rigour and candour. Accurate about what the product does and does not yet do, and prepared to say so.
  • Practical disposition. Willing to work hands on with hardware and vehicles, at our facility and at customer sites.

Desirable

  • Experience of remote management protocols for charging equipment.
  • Experience of off highway, heavy vehicle or industrial electrification, where implementation of standards is less uniform than in passenger vehicles.
  • Background in battery management, energy storage or energy management systems.
  • Experience of bidirectional charging or vehicle to grid applications.
  • Experience of product conformity and certification for electrical equipment.
  • Knowledge of cyber security and certificate management for connected charging equipment.
  • Participation in industry standards or interoperability bodies.
  • Experience of an early stage or scaling engineering organisation.

Please note that at this time we are unable to provide UK visa sponsorship

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. title: OPUS-team søger ny kollega til primærbehandlerfunktion på Psykiatrisk Center Nordsjælland
description:
OPUS-teamet skal udvides, og deraf står vi overfor en opnormering. Vi søger derfor en ergoterapeut, fysioterapeut eller en sygeplejersker med primærbehandlerfunktion til at indgå i vores tværfaglige behandlingsteam.

Du skal kunne arbejde selvstændigt og terapeutisk ud fra den kognitive adfærdsterapeutiske (KAT) referenceramme. Det vil være en fordel at kende til KAT i nogen udstrækning, men er ikke et krav i sig selv. Du vil blive tilbudt kurser og undervisning heri. Et vist kendskab til psykopatologi vil ligeledes være en fordel.

Rollen og hverdagen som primærbehandler i OPUS

OPUS er et 2-årigt ambulant behandlingstilbud til unge voksne (fra 18 til 35 år) med debuterende psykotiske lidelser, herunder skizofreni og skizotypi. Behandlingen indledes med diagnostisk udredning og tager udgangspunkt i kognitive terapeutiske principper. Behandlingen indeholder både medicinsk behandling, individuelle samtaler hos primærbehandler og gruppeforløb som f.eks.: Psykoedukation både til patienter og pårørende, social-færdighedstræning (SFT), flerfamiliegruppe, kropsbevidsthed og afspænding og selvværdsgruppe. Desuden lægges der stor vægt på pårørende- og netværk inddragelse i det enkelte patientforløb.

Primærbehandleren har en koordinerende funktion i forhold til interne behandlingstilbud (sengeafsnit, Bostedsteamet og F-ACT), samt eksterne samarbejdspartnere (f.eks. jobcentre, socialforvaltning, socialpsykiatriske tilbud og evt. uddannelsestilbud).

Det tværfaglige team du kommer til at samarbejde med, består af to sekretærer, to overlæger, 1-2 læger i uddannelse i psykiatri, derudover 17 Primærbehandlere fordelt over følgende faggrupper: psykologer, oversygeplejerske, sygeplejersker, fysioterapeut, ergoterapeuter og socialrådgivere. Dertil kommer en recovery mentor.

Alle, med undtagelse af overlæger og sekretær, arbejder individuelt som primærbehandler med ”egne” patienter og har et case load på ca. 15 patienter. Primærbehandleren fungerer også som ” case maneger”

I gruppeforløbene arbejder du altid sammen med en anden behandler.

Det forventes, at primærbehandleren deltager aktivt i teamkonferencer, teammøder, sparring og supervisioner og bidrager med viden, nysgerrighed og faglig kompetence. Det forventes desuden, at primærbehandleren holder sig løbende orienteret indenfor sit fagområde, herunder deltagelse i undervisning, kurser og evt. efteruddannelse.

Der er i afsnittet løbende kognitiv supervision, faglig sparring, undervisning samt teamkonferencer. Desuden vil der i opstartsfasen være introduktion og du blive tilknyttet to mentorer.

Vi forventer, at du

  • Har psykiatrisk erfaring og interesse for arbejdet med patienter med psykose lidelser/skizofreni
  • Har lyst og evne til at arbejde individuelt og selvstændigt
  • Har lyst og evne til at indgå i det tværfaglige behandlingsteam
  • Har uddannelse indenfor, eller kendskab til, det kognitive adfærdsterapeutiske område
  • Har interesse for undervisning og psykoedukation
  • Har lyst til at arbejde med patienter i gruppeforløb, i samarbejde med kollega
  • Er fleksibel i forhold til arbejdstid (Ambulatoriet har åbnet i dagstiden, men enkelte pårørende grupper ligger udenfor normal arbejdstid.)
  • Har autorisation som sygeplejerske (hvis du er uddannet sygeplejerske)

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår
Stillingen er på 37 timer og er til besættelse pr**. 1. november 2026 eller efter aftale.**

Ambulatoriet har åbent mandag til fredag. Din arbejdstid vil derfor primært ligge inden for dette tidsrum.

Som ergoterapeut eller fysioterapeut ansættes du i henhold til overenskomst for ikke-ledende ergoterapeuter, fysioterapeuter og jordmædre. Du er under ansættelsen omfattet af den til enhver tid gældende arbejdstidsaftale indgået mellem Regionernes Lønings- og Takstnævn og Ergoterapeutforeningen.

Regionen er et døgndækket område, og du vil efter konkret behov kunne blive planlagt med vagter uden for ambulatoriets åbningstider i overensstemmelse med reglerne i den gældende arbejdstidsaftale.

Er du sygeplejerske ansættes du i henhold til overenskomst for ikke-ledende personale på Sundhedskartellets område. Du er under ansættelsen omfattet af den til enhver tid gældende arbejdstidsaftale indgået mellem Regionernes Lønnings- og Takstnævn og Dansk Sygeplejeråd.

Som nyansat sygeplejrske bliver du i øvrigt knyttet til et specifikt døgnafsnit, hvor du indgår i vagtarbejder lørdag og søndag hver 6. uge. Vi sørger naturligvis for at klæde dig godt på til opgaven. Det sker i form af individuelt introprogram, vidensdeling og sparring med kollegaer. Og så sker det i form af løbende kompetenceudvikling med afsæti dine erfaringer og behov.

Ansøgningsprocedure
Hvis du vil vide mere om stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte fysioterapeut/primærbehandler Anette Schifter-Holm på tlf. 21 35 18 90 eller ergoterapeut Rikke Sonnenborg Christensen på mail rikke.sonnenborg.christensen@regionh.dk.

Ansøgningsfristen er den 01. september 2026.

Vi forventer at afholde samtaler d. 10.09 og/eller d. 11.09

Ansøgning, CV, uddannelsesbevis og relevante dokumenter sendes online via linket her på siden.

Yderligere oplysninger om Psykiatrisk Center Nordsjælland findes på Psykiatri i Region Hovedstaden.

title: Electrical Estimator
description:

In this role, you will be responsible for developing accurate, competitive cost estimates for large scale commercial and industrial electrical projects. You will analyze project documents, drawings, and specifications to prepare detailed takeoffs, pricing, and proposals that support successful project execution.

The Electrical Estimator works closely with project managers, operations, and field leadership to ensure scopes are clearly defined, risks are identified early, and budgets align with installation methods and schedules. This role requires strong analytical skills, construction knowledge, and the ability to manage multiple bids simultaneously in a fast paced environment.

Responsibilities

  • Accurately estimating costs for commercial or industrial electrical installations and efficiently managing projects from inception to completion
  • This role entails full ownership of projects from initiation to completion, with a focus on enhancing cost-estimation methods to minimize disparities between projected and actual expenses

  • Liaise with clients to understand project requirements, including pricing, invoicing, and project management tasks
  • Analyze blueprints to determine optimal wire lengths and outlet placements adhering to electrical codes
  • Research market prices to estimate material and fixture costs for electrical projects accurately
  • Review subcontractor and vendor quotes to ensure accuracy in project cost estimation
  • Assess labor requirements for each project to determine project feasibility
  • Evaluate potential profitability of electrical projects to support bidding decisions
  • Prepare and submit competitive project bids following established guidelines
  • Manage awarded projects and provide assistance in project management when not involved in estimating tasks

Qualifications

  • Ability to interpret blueprints accurately

title: Community Project Officer - 2 year FTC
description:
Help shape community-led projects that build lasting, positive change in North Kensington.

As a Community Project Officer, you'll play a key role in supporting our residents and working alongside local community organisations to deliver meaningful, long-term recovery by championing grassroots initiatives and projects helping residents turn their priorities and ideas into lasting, positive change.

Working Style

You'll be based in the Borough for 4 days a week, playing a key role in serving the local community. Whether you're meeting community partners or working with resident panels, you'll be part of a dedicated team making a real difference to residents' lives.

What you'll be doing

Your work will focus on coordinating and delivering key programmes including the Grenfell Projects Fund and the Community Leadership Programme in North Kensington Day-to-day, you'll meet with local community groups to review progress, monitoring their delivery and help them overcome delivery challenges and manage budgets and grant outcomes and outputs to ensure projects remain compliant and on track. You'll also gather and analyse both qualitative and quantitative performance data, using case studies and feedback to demonstrate the real-world impact of community initiatives, using software such as Monday.com, Plinth and Microsoft applications.

Working closely with resident panels, , Council teams and external partners, you'll prepare clear reports, briefings and presentations for a range of audiences. This will include attending out-of-hours community meetings to listen directly to residents and help shape new initiatives. You'll manage project plans, finance systems and risk logs across multiple programmes simultaneously, balancing community expectations with available resources in a sensitive environment with care and competence.

For further details, please review the Job Description and Person Specification

What you'll bring

You'll bring experience managing community, regeneration, public sector or voluntary sector programmes, with a proven track record in project management, grant administration and co-designing projects alongside local communities. You'll have strong skills in gathering and evaluating data to evidence impact, alongside confidence using digital tools for project tracking and reporting.

You'll bring exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to write clear briefings and build trust across diverse audiences. Working in a sensitive environment requires high emotional intelligence, political awareness, discretion and resilience under pressure. You'll be highly organised, solution-oriented and adept at supporting smaller organisations with governance and finance while balancing competing priorities fairly and respectfully.

Most importantly, you're someone who approaches sensitive challenges with empathy, patience and practical solutions-deeply committed to supporting grassroots delivery and building genuine relationships across the community.

Why join us

At RBKC, we're all in - investing in our people, our communities and our future.

You'll join a supportive, collaborative team where knowledge is shared and your efforts contribute directly to community recovery and long-term positive impact. We offer continuous professional development and training to support your career growth, alongside flexible working arrangements to help you balance your work and life.

Alongside a competitive salary, you'll benefit from thorough wellbeing support, employee perks and a working environment where your contribution to the borough is genuinely valued.

About us

Kensington and Chelsea is home to diverse communities, thriving businesses and unique local places. Everything we do is focused on supporting our residents, strengthening our approach and creating a fairer borough.

As a competent and caring Council, we take pride in our work every day, ensuring our services are delivered with care and competence. We listen to our residents, act with integrity and work together to build a borough that is greener, safer and fairer for all.

In this role, you'll be a vital champion for community recovery - bringing an empathetic, dedicated approach to supporting residents and local groups. Supporting Grenfell recovery takes place in a complex and heavily scrutinised environment where work isn't always plain sailing. However, your calm and thoughtful approach will help build trust, navigate sensitive challenges and turn obstacles into vital opportunities for lasting community improvement.

Interview Details & Role Requirements

Interviews will be held in person on week commencing 21st September 2026

This is a 2 year FTC

Ready to join us?

We're all in - are you? If you share our values and have the skills to contribute, we'd love to hear from you.

Please apply online explaining how you meet the requirements set out in the person specification and job description.

We reserve the right to extend or close this vacancy early without warning subject to the volume of suitable applicants.

We are committed to promoting equality and respecting diversity and welcome applications from all sections of the community.

We are a Disability Confident Employer - committed to ensuring that our recruitment and selection process is inclusive and accessible.

In this role, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor, helping public and private sector customers design secure, resilient, and practical technology solutions across the enterprise data center stack, including compute, storage, networking, virtualization, cloud, and security.   • Proven ability to translate complex technical concepts for both technical and non‑technical audiences
  • Experience responding to formal procurement processes, including RFPs, RFIs, and RFQs, particularly within public sector or regulated industries
  • Excellent presentation, communication, and relationship‑building skills
  • Relevant industry certifications strongly preferred, including CISSP, CISM, Security+, or vendor-specific security certifications from organizations such as Palo Alto Networks, Cisco, or Fortinet
  • Prior experience supporting public sector customers alongside private enterprise customers preferred
  • Existing professional network within enterprise security or infrastructure communities preferred
  • Experience mentoring or leading a technical pre‑sales team preferred

Additional Requirements

  • Ability to function effectively in both pre‑sales and post‑sales engagements
  • Ability to build trusted relationships with customers and internal stakeholders
  • Willingness to pursue and maintain partner vendor certifications as required

title: Engineering Lead
description:
About KIRA

Our mission is to make money smart, reliable and within reach for everyone.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in Asia and it includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and at ease and self reliance, become an expert. We believe AI will help us achieve this in our generation.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

KIRA builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Engineering Lead owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems. This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

What You'll Own

  • Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

  • Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

  • Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

  • Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

  • Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

  • Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

Nice to have

  • Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

  • Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Senior Fullstack Developer (PHP)
description:
Bold ideas need dependable infrastructure, and the people who can build and maintain it. At Qu, we operate sovereign, in-country infrastructure across data centres, cloud, and managed services, so Canada's builders and innovators can move fast without surrendering control. Infrastructure for the inspired.

Why Qu

Qu is built by people who value craft, humility, collaboration, and follow-through. Small by design, 120 people, your voice carries and your impact shows. You will work on real problems that matter, ensuring our customers have what they need when they need it, so they can focus on growth.

The role

We Are Growing The Engineering Team Behind Our Core Platform, And We Are Looking For a Strong Senior Fullstack Developer, Comfortable Across The Front End, Back End, And Database Layer, Who Can Also Engage Thoughtfully With Our Broader Data Architecture As It Evolves. Working With Our Technical Lead, You Will

  • Build and modernize our applications fullstack in PHP 8, with React front ends, applying solid engineering practice: version control, CI/CD, Linux, and Qu's own testing practices.
  • Work confidently on the database side of that fullstack, including writing and tuning efficient SQL Server queries and supporting the reliability, performance, and security of our data.
  • Stay involved in and knowledgeable about our data architecture as it evolves, including how our systems share and integrate data, working alongside others rather than owning that architecture alone.
  • Use AI as a core part of how you build, or be ready to learn and grow comfortable with that quickly, working within the way we build with AI here (more below).
  • Automate and integrate across the Microsoft ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Power Platform, Power Automate).

How We Work, Including With AI

We build with AI as a core part of how we work, but it amplifies strong engineering, it does not replace it. You are independently excellent: you can design, write, and debug in PHP and SQL on your own, without leaning on a tool. On top of that, you use AI the way we do, deliberately and consistently, to accelerate delivery. You drive it, you verify everything it produces, and code review stays non-negotiable. We work within a company AI use policy and governance framework, and you are comfortable operating inside clear guardrails like these, and can stand up new AI-assisted workflows responsibly within them. If that is already how you build, you will fit in fast.

What You Bring

Must have

  • Senior fullstack PHP (8.x) development, with genuine SQL proficiency you own independently of any AI tool.
  • Strong Microsoft SQL Server: writing and tuning queries, schema design, and stored procedures.
  • Solid engineering foundations: Git, CI/CD, and Linux, and an understanding of Qu's testing practices.
  • The AI-assisted way of working described above, or the willingness to learn it and grow comfortable with it quickly: AI for acceleration, not replacement, with the judgment to know where and how to apply it.

Strong assets

  • Database administration depth: replication, backup and recovery, performance tuning, high availability, and security.
  • Exposure to data architecture concepts: shared data models and integrating data cleanly across multiple systems.
  • Cloud and virtualization (VMs, cloud platforms) and infrastructure-aware development.
  • React front end (TypeScript, Tailwind).
  • Microsoft 365 and Power Platform / Power Automate proficiency.
  • Working awareness of AI governance, safety, and current trends.

Nice to have

  • ColdFusion / Lucee.
  • Data centre domain knowledge: colocation, cloud, networking, and capacity.

Who Thrives Here

This is a wide role by design. The person who succeeds is a strong fullstack developer who is just as comfortable on the database side, stays engaged with how our data fits together at a broader level, switches context without losing quality, and takes real ownership on a small team where the work is visible and the stakes are real.

Life at Qu

Mentorship, comprehensive health coverage, retirement savings, paid time off, learning budgets, and wellness resources, along with flexible scheduling for 24/7 teams.

title: Frontend Developer
description:
Full-time


Important:


There is no relocation assistance. Only apply if you are within commuting distance or will self-relocate.


Are you a frontend developer who wants to do more than build another marketing website or CRUD app? We're building a next-generation distributed operating system for a major Fortune 100 client. Our stack is Linux + Java + React. We've built extensive tooling, ported to half a dozen hardware platforms, and published an extensive SDK for external developers. We recently built a custom beverage dispenser from scratch – including a custom circuit board and 3D-printed parts – just to exercise our software stack.


What You'll Be Working On – You'll join our team as a frontend developer contributing to a React/TypeScript SDK platform that powers touchscreen applications on connected embedded devices, including dispensers. Your work will be used by third-party development partners to build real, deployed experiences – meaning you're building for developers as much as end users.
Who Should Apply – New grads with a strong portfolio and genuine curiosity who are interested in meaningful, technically interesting work on a platform used in the real world, as well as direct mentorship from a senior architect with 30 years of experience and 15+ years in React/TypeScript, all the while working with a small team where your contributions are visible and your voice matters. Intermediate developers (2–5 years of experience) with production React/TypeScript experience are an ideal fit. If you've built something you're proud of - a side project, an open-source contribution, a polished portfolio piece – we want to see it. That said, you should bring:

Requirements


Solid foundation in React and TypeScript - you don't need to be a 10-year veteran, but you should be comfortable in a typed codebase and care about API design


Curiosity about how things work under the hood - our platform sits at the intersection of web tech and embedded Linux, familiar but different enough to be interesting.


Strong communication skills - we're a small, senior team, and clear communication goes a long way


Bonus points if you have experience with monorepo tooling (NX, Turborepo), Web Components, component library authoring, or interest in IoT or embedded systems.


Responsibilities


Day-to-day work includes building and maintaining UI SDK components, contributing to a developer tooling platform, and collaborating on a design system purpose-built for embedded environments.


Build, maintain, and document React/TypeScript SDK components designed for use by third-party developers on embedded touchscreen devices


Contribute to a developer-facing tooling platform, including APIs, configuration surfaces, and DX improvements


Collaborate on a design system purpose-built for constrained embedded environments (limited screen size, performance budgets, input constraints)


Partner with a senior architect to make API design decisions that balance flexibility for partners with consistency across the SDK


Write and maintain component documentation and usage examples to support third-party developer adoption


Contribute to testing strategies appropriate for embedded UI (unit, integration, and potentially device-level testing)


Engage with third-party development partners to understand how the SDK is being used in the wild and feed that back into the platform

and development.

title: Geotechnical Intern (Summer 2027)
description:

Are you looking to further your education with intensive, real-world experience and mentorship from professional engineers? Do you like the idea of spending this summer outdoors, getting your hands dirty (literally) while you learn about what it takes to be a successful geotechnical engineer? title: Project Geotechnical Engineer
description:
As a Project Geotechnical Engineer, you will play a key role in managing some of the most exciting and technically challenging projects. Responsibilities include planning field programs, conducting technical briefings with field staff, and project management tasks including budgeting and client communications. You will also be responsible for performing engineering analyses and preparing technical reports, as well as conducting regular site visits, overseeing field explorations and construction observations. As a project manager, you will be responsible for mentoring and overseeing the work of junior staff.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead or coordinate the development and implementation of field exploration programs and construction observation projects. Ensure that work performed is consistent with project plans and specifications as well as in accordance with safety guidelines.
  • Assist with training junior technical and technician staff.
  • Complete engineering analyses and calculations. Develop moderately complex conceptual models.
  • Complete moderately complex spatial analyses.
  • Lead the generation of technical reports including completion of routine reports, figures, tables, etc.; Assist senior staff in completing portions of large, complex reports, figures, tables, etc.
  • Support project management tasks such as budget planning, general field report reviews, and proposal development. Manage small projects under the supervision of a certified professional engineer or geologist as required.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering required; Master's degree with a Geotechnical Engineering focus strongly preferred.
  • Minimum 4 years of relevant experience is required.
  • At least one year of project management experience.
  • PE license required.
  • Professional-level verbal and written communication skills are a must.
  • Valid driver’s license required.

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

  • All candidates are subject to completing a background check, and reference check.
  • All candidates are required to participate in our medical surveillance program.
  • Ability to perform a wide range of physical activities and do heavy work including exerting up to 50 pounds of force on occasion.
  • Ability to perform consistent work on a PC with prolonged sitting and view of a monitor/screen.
  • Ability to travel for short-term and long-term assignments as needed.
  • All employees are responsible for conducting their work in a safe manner. This includes identifying potential safety hazards and reporting them to the designated project manager in a timely manner and participating in project safety briefings. This also includes wearing appropriate safety equipment when working in the field and completing all required health & safety training prior to beginning fieldwork.
