title: Community Mobilisation & CERT Training Officer
description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local - Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

Position Purpose:

The Community Mobilization & CERT Training Officer will lead community engagement, mobilization, and capacity-building efforts under the DRR project, with a specific focus on establishing and training Community Emergency Response Teams (CERT). The role ensures that host communities and camp populations are actively engaged, informed, and equipped with practical skills to prepare for and respond to disasters.


Key Objectives of the Position:

Community Mobilization

  • Mobilize communities/camp households to actively participate in DRR planning, activities, and awareness sessions
  • Identify and engage community leaders, volunteers, and vulnerable household representatives to support project activities
  • Facilitate the formation and functioning of community-based disaster management committees or similar structures
  • Promote inclusive participation of women, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups in DRR activities

CERT Training & Capacity Building

  • Design and deliver Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) training modules covering first aid, search and rescue basics, evacuation procedures, fire safety, and early warning response
  • Conduct simulation exercises and mock drills (e.g., landslide/flood response) with CERT members and the wider community
  • Build capacity of CERT volunteers to lead first-response actions during emergencies, prior to arrival of formal responders
  • Develop training materials, job aids, and IEC (Information, Education, Communication) content adapted to the local context and literacy levels

Awareness Raising & Preparedness

  • Conduct awareness sessions for vulnerable households on disaster risks, preparedness measures, and early warning signals
  • Support household-level and community-level contingency and evacuation planning
  • Promote child-focused DRR messaging and age-appropriate awareness activities for children in the camp

Coordination, Monitoring & Reporting

  • Coordinate closely with Site Management and Camp-in-Charge (CiC) for mobilization activities and use of common spaces/facilities
  • Maintain attendance records, training reports, and documentation of CERT formation and activities
  • Contribute updates and case information to Situation Reports (SitRep) and share with relevant channels
  • Support household-level visits to identify vulnerable families and follow up on their engagement in DRR activities
  • Participate in sectoral coordination meetings to share community mobilisation updates.


Key Responsibilities:


Training Facilitation, communications and Implementation:

  • Strong facilitation, training, and communication skills
  • Ability to build rapport and trust with diverse community groups
  • Good understanding of participatory approaches and adult learning techniques
  • Ability to work in difficult field/camp conditions and respond during emergencies
  • Proficiency in local language; working knowledge of English preferred
  • Good report-writing and documentation skills
  • Ability to work under pressure in emergency contexts and travel to field/camp locations
  • Strong interpersonal and community engagement skills
  • Manage the assigned project(s) to meet the project objectives within budget, set time frame, quality, and standards
  • Develop and implement an appropriate and effective project strategy, setting clear objectives and indicators, for Livelihoods & entrepreneurship development activities in consultation with other staff and youth and women entrepreneurs and, where appropriate, with the local communities
  • Mainstream protection, accountability, gender, disability, and environmental protection
  • All documents guiding implementation, such as budgets, DIPs, and projections, are prepared, updated, and used correctly
  • Ensure needs assessments and surveys are conducted, data analyzed, and suggestions made for appropriate interventions as needed.
  • Regular monitoring and reporting of project implementation.
  • Timely Submission of quality narrative reports to the line manager on project progress, program team, and donors.

Staff Management:

  • Line manages the staff(s) of the assigned project(s), including day-to-day management, development and training etc.
  • Take responsibility for discussing job expectations; appraise performance against set objectives regularly.
  • Overall responsibility for staff work plans, vacation schedules, and development activities, and maintain a professional and open relationship with team members, promoting a strong spirit and providing oversight and guidance to allow for successful team performance.
  • Staff coaching and supervision for their development.

Coordination and networking:

  • Maintain and create strategic partnerships and networks with donors, the UN, and other NGOs.
  • Actively participate in Cluster meetings to ensure WV programming information is shared and requests for cluster mechanisms are responded to.
  • Keep and share information from NGO meetings, government correspondence, and internal World Vision Lessons Learned.
  • Ensure that World Vision is represented in coordination forums and review meetings.
  • Foster formal government at all levels and community engagement and coordination

Financial Management:


  • Manage the DRR assignment project and ensure all expenses are according to budget and meet donor standards for financial management, including accountability and good governance.
  • Manage the program budget through the passing of timely orders, the preparation of monthly forecasts, and the monitoring of expenditure.

Spiritual Leadership:


  • Exhibit spiritual maturity, integrity, and a dynamic personal sense of life calling



Knowledge, Skill & Experience:

Required Education, training, license, registration, and/or Certification:


  • Bachelor's degree in social science, Development Studies, Disaster Management, or related field

  • Minimum 2–3 years of experience in community mobilization, social/community work, or CERT/first responder training
  • Certification or training experience in CERT, first aid, or emergency response preferred
  • Experience working with displaced/camp populations and child protection principles is an advantage
  • CERT Basic Training and/or Training of Trainers (ToT), where available
  • First Aid/CPR certification
  • Incident Command System (ICS) or emergency coordination training
  • Community-Based Disaster Risk Reduction (CBDRR) training
  • Relevant UNDRR DRR courses and certifications


  • Knowledge of DRR & Climate Change Adaptation Intervention, System Strengthening & Networking, Livelihood, Group Management, etc.
  • Reporting and accounting experience needed
  • Experience in project implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and report writing.
  • Good at communication, interpersonal skills, and cross-cultural sensitivity.
  • Familiar with the various tools used in the field for program monitoring
  • Excellent English communication skills (oral and written)
  • Knowledge of MS Office, websites, Outlook, and Lotus Notes
  • Commitment to World Vision Core Values and Mission Statement
  • Ability to exhibit exemplary lifestyle as interpreted in a specific local culture context
  • Agreement with World Vision’s ethos
  • Cross-cultural sensitivity, flexible world view, emotional maturity, and physical stamina


Required Language(s): English, Bangla and Rohingya


Required travel and/or work environment accommodations:


Must be willing and able to travel working are/in the country

Some project locations may be in remote areas. Staff are expected to live in the location for short periods

Committed to World Vision Ethos, Mission, Vision, and Core Values

Salary: Negotiable


Compensation & Other Benefits:


Provident fund, Gratuity, Festival Bonus: 1, Other benefits as per organizations policy.


Employment Status: Full Time


World Vision is committed to first do no harm to children or adult beneficiaries, to respect the rights of all beneficiaries, and to uphold the best interests of children as a primary consideration in all actions and decisions: accordingly, all the recruits will go through specific checks and compliance procedures in accordance to its Child and Adult Safeguarding Policy.

title: Digital Product Manager
description:
Believ: ABOUT US

At Believ, formerly known as Liberty Charge, we believe sustainable transport should be accessible to everyone. We’re a Charge Point Operator (CPO) on a mission to create the UK’s most reliable electric vehicle charging network that doesn’t cost the earth and leaves no one behind.

We work closely with local authorities and businesses to deliver reliable, high-quality charging networks at pace, at scale and at zero cost.

We offer all the advantages of being a scale-up business, but with the added security and long-term backing from well-known parents - Liberty Global (who also own our delivery partner, Virgin Media O2) and Zouk Capital (who manage the Government’s Charging Investment Infrastructure Fund).

You’ll be joining this exciting journey at the start of our scale-up phase, and work with us to hit the ambitious targets our shareholders have set. You’ll become part of a passionate and supportive in-house cross functional Tech team of 15 people, working on-site 3 days a week, following agile and lean best practices.

About the role
We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Digital Product Manager to drive and improve our digital product portfolio, spanning both internal and external interfaces. Reporting to the Head of Digital Product, this role will partner closely with Engineering and UX/UI leadership to deliver market-leading digital solutions that directly contribute to company-wide targets including utilisation and customer satisfaction. You will own the digital product management for one of our Engineering squads - spanning roadmap creation through to delivery - and will play a key role in influencing and implementing the product direction. Your immediate focus will be delivering a cutting-edge consumer-facing EV charging app and internal platform, while contributing to the entire digital product portfolio to identify and prioritise opportunities for innovation and value creation.

Responsibilities:

  • Support the implementation of the digital product strategy across the portfolio of internal and external digital products.
  • Own the feature request intake process for the squad, evaluating and translating requests and business objectives into a coherent, prioritised roadmap.
  • Track success metrics tied to company targets, including product utilisation, CSAT, and retention, using data to drive continuous improvement.
  • Iterate and improve on the product development lifecycle for digital interfaces, from ideation and requirements gathering to design, development, testing, and launch.
  • Contribute to the product discovery process, maintaining a healthy pipeline of validated opportunities ahead of delivery.
  • Conduct competitive analysis, market validation and review user research to surface user needs, pain points, and opportunities.
  • Partner with Engineering and UX/UI leadership to ensure alignment on product vision, strategy, and execution.
  • Develop detailed product requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria to guide the development process and ensure the successful delivery of high-quality products.
  • Work with cross-functional teams to ensure timely and effective delivery of product features, managing timelines, resources, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Continuously monitor and analyse product performance, user feedback, and key metrics to inform data-driven decisions and iterative improvements.

Qualifications:

  • Experience in product management, with a track record of delivering successful digital products -- ideally in technology, automotive, or a related field.
  • Deep understanding of user-centered design principles, Agile/Scrum methodologies, and modern product management practices.
  • Strong analytical and decision-making skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information, make data-driven calls, and clearly communicate the strategic reasoning behind them to stakeholders.
  • Strong communicator and influencer, with the ability to align cross-functional teams.
  • Experience using product analytics, user research, and A/B testing to drive decisions - and a track record of building more data-informed ways of working within a team.
  • Passion for sustainability, clean energy, and environmental stewardship.

Skills and Abilities:

  • Able to manage multiple priorities and deliverables in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Able to translate the Product vision into actionable product requirements and roadmaps that guide execution from concept through to delivery.
  • Proficiency in product management and collaboration tools such as JIRA, Confluence, Trello, or similar.
  • Experience with mobile app development frameworks, technologies, and best practices, with the ability to collaborate effectively with engineering and design teams.
  • A drive to contribute to a strong product culture - championing user empathy, data-informed decisions, and continuous improvement as the way the team works day to day.
  • Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail, with a focus on delivering high-quality products that meet user needs and exceed expectations.

Additional Knowledge and Skills (Desirable):

  • Experience in the EV charging industry or related fields, with an understanding of industry trends, challenges, and opportunities.
  • Knowledge of regulatory compliance requirements and industry standards related to EV charging and digital interfaces.
  • Familiarity with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure) and integration technologies (e.g., APIs, websockets) to support seamless digital experiences.
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams in a regulated industry, such as energy, transportation, or utilities, with an understanding of industry-specific challenges and opportunities.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business, Marketing, Computer Science, or a related field.

About you

At Believ, we are building a culture that attracts and retains the best talent. We are a dedicated and high-performing team, accustomed to working at pace in an ever-evolving industry, and we are looking for people who are as passionate as us about cutting carbon emissions and providing cleaner air for all. The successful candidate will have the following attributes and skills:

  • Ability to balance commercial and customer objectives
  • Consumer focused
  • Willingness to learn in a new industry
  • Have a strong interest in sustainability
  • Be able to shift from set strategy should industry change direction
  • Excellent communicator & strong interpersonal skills

Interview process

  • Initial briefing with our recruiter
  • Initial screening online
  • Technical assessment and meeting the broader team in the office in Southwark

Location

The business is currently based in our head offices in Southwark. The position is full-time hybrid position (3 days in the office per week).

Believ is an equal opportunity employer. We embrace diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for our people.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

If you don’t meet every requirement but are excited by the role, we’d still love to hear from you.

title: Lead Quality Engineer - Data
description:
Job Description

Lead Data Quality Engineer is responsible for creating and executing comprehensive data testing strategies and solutions, with focus on data validation, integrity testing, and quality assurance across data platforms and interfaces. This role ensures accurate test data delivery in a fast-paced environment while providing technical expertise and mentorship to team members. The position bridges data testing assurance with data engineering, architecture, and business teams to deliver robust, trustworthy data testing & test data solutions in a dynamic financial services environment.

What Will You Do?

  • Develop and execute comprehensive data testing strategies and automated testing solutions for data validation across multiple platforms, interfaces, and ETL processes
  • Design and implement automated data testing scripts and frameworks to validate data accuracy, completeness, consistency, and conformance to business rules
  • Create and maintain test management documentation; define, track, and report on quality metrics
  • Review and enhance data testing strategies for new and existing data initiatives;
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into executable testing scenarios and validation rules
  • Manage defect tracking workflows and coordinate resolution with development and business teams
  • Work closely with vendors to implement testing solutions
  • Recommend improvements to testing processes, technology, and interfaces that improve the effectiveness of testing teams
  • Own test data management strategy and automation; ensure test data is properly provisioned, maintained, and compliant with data governance policies

Must have:

  • 6+ years of hands-on experience in data testing and validation across various data platforms, interfaces, and data warehouses
  • 5+ years of experience working with and testing relational databases; ability to write and test complex SQL queries and stored procedures
  • Strong proficiency with data testing and validation tools (DVO, QuerySurge, or similar frameworks) and data profiling tools (IDC/CDGC or equivalent)
  • Strong understanding of data models, ER diagrams, and ability to analyze complex data mapping and business rule documentation
  • Experience in ETL Tools like IICS, Informatica Power Center or similar and ETL scheduler tools
  • Proven experience in test data management strategy, provisioning, and automation; understanding of data governance and compliance requirements
  • Proven ability mentoring team members (onshore & offshore) and providing technical direction
  • Proficiency with Git version control, branching strategies, and strong experience testing and working in continuous delivery (CICD) environment.
  • Experience with test management tools (Azure Test Plans, Jira QMetry) and quality metrics reporting

Nice‑to‑have

  • Knowledge about data obfuscation routines
  • Experience using AI tools like Copilot for test design or test automation

Job Description

Qualifications

title: Instructional Designer- Partner Specific
description:
This position is not open to applicants residing in or otherwise based in California, New York, Illinois, or Massachusetts. Additionally, applicants must be located in the Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific time zones.

Note to Applicants

We’re looking for professionals who take pride in their work. We know your resume tells part of the story, but our application questions help us understand how you think and work. Because we receive a high volume of applications, only applications with complete, thoughtful responses will be reviewed.

Given the AI restriction on this engagement, described below, we ask that your responses be your own work.

Engagement Details

This is instructional design work, with a twist.

Every project starts with an existing course and a charter that defines exactly what is changing about it. The work is reading that charter closely, translating it into specific revisions in specific places, and executing them cleanly on a short, fixed cycle, without drifting into the parts of the course the charter does not cover.

It calls on the full instructional design skill set: learning theory, alignment, assessment design, accessibility, and SME collaboration. What is distinctive is where the difficulty sits. The hard calls here are about scope and defensibility: deciding what a charter line means in practice, and documenting why you drew the line where you did. It also means finding things you would want to change and leaving them alone. If your instinct when you open a course is to fix everything you find, this engagement will frustrate you. If you can see all of it and still deliver only what the charter covers, documenting the rest for the partner, you should do well here.

You will work with Subject Matter Experts and coordinate with internal teams, including Editorial and Quality Review, ensuring every revision adheres to research-based practice and partner-defined quality standards.

This engagement carries a partner data restriction. No partner course content, materials, or partner-provided information may be entered into, uploaded to, or processed by any AI system, internal or external, at any point during the engagement.

This is an independent contractor engagement (1099). Contractors are free to work with other clients, and accepting one project carries no obligation to accept another. Meeting times are set in advance around each project’s milestones. Outside of those scheduled meetings and agreed deadlines, you determine your own working hours and process for completing the work.

Scope of Work

  • Complete a scoped review of the assigned course and map the charter to specific course locations, documenting cascading effects, assumptions, and ambiguities before development begins.
  • Deliver a specific list of items requiring SME input before the first working session.
  • Collaborate with SMEs to revise instruction and assessments in scope, aligned to learning outcomes and the charter, while documenting anything outside scope rather than addressing it.
  • Suggest relevant open educational resources and instructional methods appropriate to the revision.
  • Maintain comprehensive documentation of design decisions to support partner review and approval.
  • Incorporate partner and stakeholder feedback through agreed revision cycles.
  • Facilitate SME working sessions to obtain the approvals required to complete deliverables.
  • Coordinate with internal teams at defined handoff points to ensure deliverables are completed on schedule.
  • Complete self-QA before each handoff and deliver complete, accurate work by each fixed milestone.
  • Submit a status update with each milestone deliverable, and flag anything that's off track as soon as you identify it, so downstream stakeholders aren't caught by surprise.
  • Work from the version of the design standards and charter in effect for your project. Both may be revised between projects as the program evolves.

What You Need to Get the Job Done

  • Advanced degree in Education, Instructional Technology, or a related field.
  • Current, in-depth knowledge of instructional design and learning theories, with expertise in online learning, instructional design and technology, adult learning theory, and andragogy/pedagogy.
  • Demonstrated experience (3-5 years) collaborating with SMEs on online course development in higher education or corporate environments.
  • Proven ability to build strong working relationships with SMEs while moving projects forward and meeting deadlines.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to lead and influence collaboratively, including holding a scope boundary professionally.
  • Ability to read a scope document and identify not just what it says, but what it means in practice: what it touches, what it doesn’t, and what’s ambiguous.
  • Strong independent judgment: the ability to make a clean, documented, defensible decision on an ambiguous question without needing every call reviewed.
  • Experience with ADA compliance and quality standards for course design (e.g., Quality Matters, OLC).
  • Competency navigating various LMS systems such as Brightspace, D2L, Canvas, Moodle, etc.
  • Ability to recognize AI-generated material in SME submissions and evaluate it critically against design standards and learning objectives.
  • Ability to pick up a revised standard or specification between projects and apply it accurately, without a ramp-up period.
  • Strong organizational skills, excellent follow-through, and exceptional attention to detail.

Is This Engagement Right for You?

  • Trust that addressing what’s in scope serves the student better than expanding into what isn’t.
  • Naturally front-load your prep, arriving at meetings with a plan rather than still forming one.
  • Can hold a professional boundary on scope with a SME without straining the relationship.
  • Comfortable working without AI assistance on partner content.
  • Deliver complete, accurate work on a hard deadline, consistently.
  • Communicate proactively, especially when something is going wrong.
  • Pick up a revised standard between projects and apply it, without defaulting back to the previous version.

What Will Make Us REALLY Love You

  • A proven track record of working with academic and business partners to create engaging and effective online courses.
  • Excellent oral/written communication and presentation skills.
  • Background in Learner Experience Design.
  • Expertise in competency-based learning.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of available open educational resources (OERs).
  • Quality assurance training and certification (QM, OSCQR, other).
  • Post-secondary teaching and learning experience.

Facility / Infrastructure Maintenance

  • Support the operation and maintenance of physical security systems, including Access Control Systems (ACS) and Video Management Systems (VMS).
  • Investigate and resolve security system faults, condition reports, and operational issues in accordance with site standards and procedures.
  • Support preventive maintenance programs, system patching, upgrades, and lifecycle management activities.

  • Support continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance procedures, system effectiveness, and operational performance.
  • Assist in ensuring security processes are consistently applied across the site.

Collaboration

  • Partner with security stakeholders and operational teams to support maintenance activities, system upgrades, and infrastructure projects.
  • Coordinate security activities that may impact facility operations, customer environments, or infrastructure deployments.
  • Support cross-functional initiatives related to new builds, site expansions, and operational improvements.
  • Share knowledge and provide operational support to colleagues and stakeholders when required.
  • Contribute recommendations that improve security operations, infrastructure resilience, and customer experience.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • High school diploma, technical certification, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Typically 2–4 years of experience in physical security, data center operations, critical infrastructure, security systems, or a related technical environment.

Duties: Perform mechanical engineering activities and execute deliverables for GeoEngineers’ trenchless engineering projects involving HDD (Horizontal Directional Drilling) and which require complex mechanical tools/equipment to bore, expand, drill, clear, and install horizontally constructed pipelines, including specialized drill rigs and drill bits, Bottom Hole Assemblies (BHAs), jetting assemblies, mud motors, flycutters, hole openers, barrel reamers, pullback assemblies, rollers, roller cradles, excavators, cranes, sidebooms, pneumatic hammers, and other specialized mechanical equipment for buoyance control, drilling fluid management, surveying, steering, etc. Specific position duties include:

· Analyze proposed trenchless crossings to determine the mechanical equipment and construction methods needed to successfully install a trenchless pipeline crossing.

· Analyze pipe stresses with product pipe mechanical properties, drilling fluid pressures, formation limit pressures, and geometric constraints for trenchless pipeline crossings. Modify/revise plans and equipment as needed based on analysis.

· Analyze mechanical soil properties derived from laboratory testing to for project planning, including recommendations for the use of specialized mechanical equipment based on soil properties.

· Produce HDD plan/profile designs, engineering calculations, and equipment layouts.

· Prepare technical proposals, project estimates, and bid documents that incorporate mechanical engineering analysis and mechanical equipment needs.

· Deliver daily reporting, budget tracking, and field engineering support on HDD projects involving complex mechanical equipment.

· Oversee mechanical engineering aspects of HDD projects from pre-construction through final closeout.

· Develop and maintain baseline HDD project schedules, monitor daily progress, and coordinate with subcontractors and subconsultants.

· Serve as a technical resource for clients and project staff on mechanical engineering considerations for HDD projects; provides guidance and expertise to solve complex challenges.

· Manage HDD project budgets, tracked expenses, identified deviations, and implemented risk mitigation.

· Maintain complete project documentation: submittals, drawings, change orders, and project closeout packages.

· Review deliverables from staff and mid-level employees such as field reports, calculations, analyses, etc. Mentor junior staff relative to technical skills, consulting best practices, mechanical equipment use and customization, etc.

· Ensure that HDD work performed is consistent with project plans and specifications and in accordance with safety guidelines.

· Complete mechanical engineering analyses and calculations. Develop complex conceptual models as needed for projects.

· Use specialized engineering software related to mechanical engineering and HDD projects.

· Investigate mechanical equipment failures on HDD projects and recommend remedies.


This position is located at GeoEngineers’ Redmond, Washington headquarters, with the option to telecommute from anywhere in the United States. Domestic travel required up to 20% of time to project sites (primarily sites in Texas and Louisiana).



Requirements: Applicants must have a Bachelor’s degree or the foreign equivalent in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related engineering field and 6 years of experience as an Engineer, Project Manager, or a closely related engineering occupation. Experience must include:

· 6 years performing engineering on projects involving HDD.

· 6 years using MathCAD, ArcGIS, MODFLOW, FLAC, Civil 3D, HEC-RAS, Plaxis, or closely related engineering software.


The position also requires:

· A Professional Engineer (PE) license.

· Completion of coursework (at either an undergraduate or graduate level) covering either Numerical Modeling or Finite Elements.

All education, training and experience may be gained concurrently. Applicants must be U.S. workers (includes U.S. citizens, permanent residents, foreign nationals granted temporary residence under one of the 1986 legalization programs, refugees, and asylees.

title: Lead Full Stack Developer
description:
We are seeking an innovative Lead Full Stack Developer (Angular, Node.js & AWS) to drive the engineering and architectural direction of our next-generation digital banking platforms. In this role, you will lead a high-performing squad of software engineers to design, build, and deploy secure, resilient, and intelligent enterprise applications.

About the Role

You will combine hands-on full stack development using Angular and Node.js with modern AWS Serverless architecture (Lambda) while integrating AI capabilities (LLM orchestrations, RAG pipelines, predictive models) directly into consumer-facing and back-office banking workflows.

Responsibilities

title: Cybersecurity SME Level II
description:
We are an employee-centric company that truly values our team members and the contributions they make to our customers and the missions they support. We pride ourselves on being forward-leaning thinkers and on building teams that are, and continue to be, technically proficient across a broad range of cyber mission areas. OneZero full-time employees receive a highly competitive benefits package, including health, dental, vision, and life insurance, a 401(k) with company matching, paid time off and holidays, an employee referral program, and educational assistance. Additional details are available on our website:

Position: Cybersecurity SME Level II

Location: Hybrid – National Capital Region (USCG Headquarters, 2703 Martin Luther King Jr. Ave SE, Washington, DC and USCG CG-C5I-Y, 7323 Telegraph Rd, Alexandria, VA)

Clearance: Active DoD SECRET (final) required

Position Summary

OneZero, LLC is seeking a Cybersecurity SME (Level II) to support a federal cybersecurity program office under an Information Assurance Risk Management Framework (IA RMF) support services contract. The Cybersecurity SME serves as a technical expert performing Information System Security Engineer (ISSE) services and cybersecurity compliance assessment, management, and reporting for federal information systems and operational technology. The SME provides insight and guidance on strategic, tactical, and operational cybersecurity plans; analyzes system and architecture requirements; recommends cybersecurity solutions; and advises on the impact of new legislation, mandates, regulations, technologies, and industry best practices.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the designated Information System Security Engineer (ISSE) for assigned USCG information systems, operational technology (OT), and hybrid cyber-physical platforms; lead the full NIST SP 800-37 RMF lifecycle from categorization through continuous monitoring and decommissioning.
  • Develop, maintain, and manage RMF authorization packages in eMASS, including SSPs, SCTMs, POA&Ms, Security Assessment Reports, Contingency Plans, Incident Response Plans, risk assessments, hardware/software lists, network topology and boundary diagrams, and data flow diagrams.
  • Perform Security Readiness Reviews (SRRs); review and analyze ACAS/Nessus vulnerability scan results; assign, track, and validate remediation through patching cycles or POA&Ms, including false-positive management and DISA ticket coordination.
  • Maintain continuous monitoring and ensure ongoing compliance with DoD, DHS, and USCG security requirements and DISA STIGs; support cATO initiatives, automated evidence collection, and dashboard integration.
  • Conduct Security Impact Assessments for proposed system changes; participate in change management boards, DHS SELC reviews, acquisition milestones (PMR, PDR, CDR), CONOPS working groups, and technical exchange meetings.
  • Integrate Zero Trust principles, RMF controls, and OT/ICS-specific security requirements into system designs; conduct security engineering analyses, trade studies, and architectural risk assessments.
  • Evaluate emerging threats, adversary TTPs, OT/ICS vulnerabilities, and supply-chain risks; recommend safeguards and mitigation strategies that reduce cyber-attack surface and enhance resilience.
  • Track and report status on authoritative orders (OPORDs, TASKORDs, FRAGOs, ALCOASTs, TCTOs) from JFHQ-DoDIN, USCYBERCOM, and CGCYBER.
  • Produce weekly, monthly, and quarterly cybersecurity readiness updates, metrics, executive-level briefings, and risk memorandums for Government leadership; respond to ad hoc cybersecurity data calls.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Cyber Security, Information Technology, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Computer Engineering, or other related technical discipline from an accredited institution. No substitution of experience for the education requirement is permitted for this labor category.
  • Minimum 6 years of related, progressive cybersecurity experience in a technical field related to this labor category.
  • DoD 8140 certification - required on the first day of performance. Must hold one of the certifications listed under Certification Requirements below (CISSP, CompTIA SecurityX/CASP+, CSSLP, CCSP, or CompTIA Cloud+), active and in good standing, before starting work. Waivers will not be granted.
  • Active final SECRET personnel security clearance (Tier 3 / SF-86 investigation)
  • Recognized expertise and technical leadership in the cybersecurity discipline, with exceptional oral and written communication skills and the ability to interface with all levels of Government management.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing the RMF, including system categorization, control selection, implementation, assessment, and continuous monitoring.
  • Core knowledge of: risk management processes; national and international cybersecurity laws, regulations, policies, and ethics; cybersecurity principles; cyber threats and vulnerabilities; computer networking concepts, protocols, and network security methodologies; and the operational impacts of cybersecurity lapses.

Certification Requirements (DoD 8140)

Cyber work roles on this task order are qualified under DoD Directive 8140.01 and DoD Manual 8140.03, Cyberspace Workforce Qualification and Management Program, which replaced DoD 8570.01-M. This position is mapped to DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role 631 – Information Systems Security Developer (ISSE) at the Intermediate proficiency level. The legacy 8570 equivalent is IASAE Level II.

Accepted certifications - the candidate must already hold one of the following:

  • CISSP - ISC2 Certified Information Systems Security Professional
  • CompTIA SecurityX - the current name for CASP+ (rebranded December 2024). Either name on a résumé refers to the same credential.
  • CSSLP - ISC2 Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional
  • CCSP - ISC2 Certified Cloud Security Professional
  • CompTIA Cloud+
  • CISSP-ISSEP or CISSP-ISSAP - exceeds this requirement and also qualifies the candidate for the Level III position

Rules that apply to every candidate:

  • The certification must be in hand before the start date. "In progress," "test scheduled," or "will obtain within 90 days" does not qualify. Per PWS Section 2.2, waivers and exceptions for contractor certifications will not be granted.
  • The certification must be active and in good standing. Ask the candidate for the certification number and expiration date, and confirm continuing education credits are current.
  • "Associate of ISC2" status does not The candidate must hold the full certification.
  • Security+ alone does not qualify for this position.
  • A higher-level certification satisfies a lower level for the same work role; a lower-level certification never satisfies a higher one.
  • If the candidate will hold privileged (administrator) access to USCG systems, they must also hold an industry certification in the technology area of focus, per the USCG Privileged User Management Program (PUMP).
  • After hire, qualification is maintained through continuous professional development - a minimum of 20 hours per year, or the continuing education required by the certification held. The Government verifies certification status through the DoD DMDC (milConnect) database.
  • Source of record for accepted qualification options is the DoD 8140 Foundational Qualification Matrix, Version 2.1 (effective 19 September 2025), published at public.cyber.mil and updated quarterly. Contract requirements may be more stringent than the matrix; the list above governs for this position.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with USCG/DoD security tools: eMASS, ACAS/Nessus/Security Center, Elastic SIEM, HBSS, Tanium, Splunk, ServiceNow, and Burp Suite.
  • Experience with OT/ICS/SCADA security, shipboard or aviation platform systems, and the DoD "Assess Only" process.
  • Familiarity with DHS 4300A, COMDTINST cybersecurity policy, DoDAF artifacts, ITIL/DESMF practices, and DevSecOps pipelines.
  • Prior USCG, DHS, or DoD RMF support experience.

Work Environment & Additional Requirements

  • Hybrid schedule: routine telework is authorized, but personnel must report on-site (hoteling) for classified (SECRET) work, SIPRNet access, meetings and events requiring presence, training, and personnel on/offboarding - at no additional cost to the Government.
  • Work schedules mirror Government staff requirements, performed within a 0600–1800 window including all core hours, Monday through Friday.
  • SIPRNet account may be required; a final SECRET clearance and NATO security briefing/read-on are prerequisites for SIPRNet access.
  • Occasional CONUS travel (and potentially Alaska, Hawaii, or U.S. Territories), including other DoD facilities and USCG vessels/aircraft; travel is COR-approved and reimbursed per the FTR/JTR.

Boddington is a flagship Newmont gold and copper operation in Western Australia, located about 130 kilometres south-east of Perth and 16 kilometres from the rural town of Boddington. You’ll strengthen Mine Control capability, improve system performance and help ensure operating practices remain aligned with site requirements and established standards.

  • Maintain and improve control room procedures, quick reference guides, training assessments and operating practices to support consistent and compliant execution.
  • Guide the response, escalation and investigation of autonomous system incidents, ensuring learnings are converted into practical improvements.
  • Analyse operational and system performance data to identify risks, constraints and opportunities that improve safety, productivity and reliability.
  • Collaborate with operations, maintenance, engineering, technical services, technology vendors and site leadership to deliver system improvements, standardise processes and support technology deployment.

  • Ability to interpret operational data, identify performance trends and translate findings into practical improvement actions.
  • Effective change, project and relationship management skills, with the ability to work across operations, maintenance, engineering, technical services and external technology providers.

This role is based at Newmont’s Boddington mine site and is offered on a 5:2, 4:3 roster. You’ll work closely with Mine Control, autonomous systems personnel, mining operations, maintenance, engineering, mine technical services, external technology providers and site leadership to support safe and effective autonomous operations.

title: Staff Geotechnical Engineer
description:
As a Staff Geotechnical Engineer, you will be responsible for several field aspects of our geotechnical services, including field exploration and observation of earthwork and foundation construction. You can expect to spend a significant portion of your time in the field on a variety of projects allowing you to develop a broad understanding of soil conditions and construction related geotechnical engineering issues. You’ll also be involved in report preparation and performing geotechnical analysis, such as slope stability, bearing capacity, settlement, deep foundation design, and seismic evaluation. This position may also provide support to our geotechnical teams in other locations as needed. This role has a preferred start date in 2027.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Responsible for field exploration and observation of earthwork and foundation construction, on projects big and small, to develop an understanding of soil conditions and construction-related geotechnical issues.
  • Responsible for preparing field reports and performing geotechnical analyses such as slope stability, bearing capacity, settlement, deep foundation design, and seismic evaluation.
  • Assists with gathering field data and field samples for related projects. Coordinates samples for testing as needed.
  • May also be responsible for providing support to our geotechnical teams at other locations as needed.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Geotechnical Engineering required; Master’s in Geotechnical or related field strongly preferred.
  • Previous internship or experience in geotechnical engineering preferred.
  • Engineer-In-Training (EIT) certification required for Staff Engineers.
  • Ability to adapt to changing project requirements and successfully work within a team.
  • Proven problem solving, and professional-level verbal and written communication skills are a must.
  • A valid driver’s license is required.
  • One year of driving experience in the United States. Consideration will be provided for international driving experience.

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

  • All candidates are subject to completing a background check, and reference check.
  • All candidates are required to participate in our medical surveillance program.
  • Ability to perform a wide range of physical activities and do heavy work including exerting up to 50 pounds of force on occasion.
  • Ability to perform consistent work on a PC with prolonged sitting and view of a monitor/screen.
  • Ability to travel for short-term and long-term assignments as needed.
  • All employees are responsible for conducting their work in a safe manner. This includes identifying potential safety hazards and reporting them to the designated project manager in a timely manner and participating in project safety briefings. This also includes wearing appropriate safety equipment when working in the field and completing all required health & safety training prior to beginning field work.

title: Staff Software Engineer – Data Systems
description:
Posted Monday, August 24, 2026 at 4:00 AM

Purpose Unlimitedis an independent financial services company with an unrelenting focus on customer-centric innovation, delivered through technology-driven solutions. Led by entrepreneur Som Seif, the company is developing a diversified product platform aimed at addressing historically underserved segments of the market. Purpose Unlimited's businesses include Purpose Investments, Advisor Solutions by Purpose, and Driven.

Vacancy Status: This is for a current vacancy

Who you are

Purpose Unlimited is building the financial products infrastructure that puts clients first,and we need the engineer who ensures that infrastructure is fast, reliable, and built to evolve. This is the Staff Engineer seat where product quality, engineering culture, and AI-era craft converge.

Youownthe hardest technical problems in our consumer-facing product.You set the standard for how code ships, how architecture decisions get made, and how AI-augmented engineering actually works in a regulated environment.Your impact is measured in productoutcomes-performance, reliability, client experience-not in lines of code or meetings attended.

We treat AI fluency as a baseline expectation, not a nice-to-have. You will lead how this team integrates AI into its engineering workflows,from AI-assisted development to governing AI-generated code in production. The routine work is increasingly handled by AI; your job is the judgment, architecture, and craft that AI cannot replace.

We use Object Process Modeling (OPM) for system mapping and Figures-of-merit (FOMs) as the measurement layer. Youdon'tneed to be a process mapping expert, but you do need to thinkinsystems,understanding how technical decisions ripple through product quality and the end-user experience.

In this role, you will

  • Design and build the core data systems that power our products, internal platforms, and AI-enabled applications.
  • Define durable data models, APIs, events, contracts, and system boundaries.
  • Build shared primitives for reliable data access, search, retrieval, synchronization, and observability.
  • Make architectural choices across databases, streaming, caching, indexing, storage, and distributed systems.
  • Design for correctness under failure: concurrency, idempotency, ordering, consistency, retries, migrations, and recovery.
  • Build data foundations that make company knowledge safely and efficiently usable by both software and AI systems.
  • Simplify complex systems and create abstractions that make other engineers faster.

You might thrive here if you

  • Have exceptional computer science fundamentals, particularly in databases, distributed systems, algorithms, and software architecture.
  • Are a strong software engineer first and can own systems from design through production.
  • Understand databases below the abstraction layer: transactions, isolation, indexing, query planning, replication, partitioning, and storage.
  • Can reason clearly about consistency, latency, throughput, durability, concurrency, and failure modes.
  • Have designed systems that cross service boundaries using APIs, events, schemas, and durable contracts.
  • Know how to choose between transactional, analytical, streaming, search, and caching systems based on first principles.
  • Understand the data requirements of modern AI systems, including retrieval, context assembly, permissions, provenance, and reliable access to structured and unstructured data.
  • Have strong taste for simple architectures and know whennotto introduce infrastructure.
  • Operate at Staff level by shaping architecture beyond your own code and raising the technical bar around you.

You could be an especially great fit if

  • You enjoy difficult problems at the intersection of backend engineering, databases, distributed systems, and emerging AI systems.
  • You have built foundational infrastructure and seen how architectural decisions behave at scale.
  • You naturally think in invariants, access patterns, state transitions, and failure cases.
  • You can move comfortably from high-level architecture to debugging a subtle systems problem.
  • You prefer a few well-designed primitives over layers of frameworks and accidental complexity.
  • What is thecanonicalrepresentation of a customer, account, portfolio, or transaction across multiple systems?
  • Where shouldstatelive, and which system should be authoritative?
  • How should an important business event propagate reliably through the system?
  • What consistency guarantees does a workflowactually require?
  • How shouldstructuredand unstructured company data be exposed safely to applications and AI systems?
  • When should something be computed synchronously, asynchronously, incrementally, or on demand?
  • How do we evolve schemas and interfaces without breaking dependent systems?

Our Five Values

  • Innovation – Bring new ideas, challenge the status quo, and experiment without waiting for permission.
  • Courage – Speak up when something isn't working; act with conviction even when it's uncomfortable.
  • Owner's Mindset – Take full accountability for your squad's outcomes.
  • Client Focus – Place client outcomes at the center of every architectural and delivery decision.
  • Winning Through Growth – Invest in your own development and actively contribute to the team's growth.

What's like here

You’lljoin a team that ships weekly, reviews each other's thinking as seriously as each other's code, and has the autonomy to make real architectural calls.We'rean engineering culture built on Owner's Mindset-you own the outcome, not just the task. We believe in Winning Through Individual and Collective Growth, which means your development matters as much as your delivery.

  • We believe in innovation and a vibrant culture- work for an innovative, people-first, financial services firm that values entrepreneurialism.
  • We believe in a flexible work structure– A flexible hybrid work model that empowers you to do your best work whether at home or the office.
  • We care about your rewards- Competitive compensation including equity program.
  • We care about your health– comprehensive group health and dental benefits and life insurance at little to no cost to you. We also offer a Lifestyle Spending Account for all your wellness needs.
  • We care about your quality of life- flexible paid time-off policy with unlimited vacation days, and flexible sick and mental health days.
  • We care about your family- Paid parental leave for eligible employees with a top-up.
  • We care about your future– Generous Group RRSP matching and an optional TFSA program.
  • We care about your development– We offer training opportunities and tuition support year-round.

You'll turn powerful AI systems into real, usable products; the kind customers and teams rely on every day. At ARC AI, we're building intelligent agents that operate in a regulated insurance environment, and your role is to make them work in the real world.

This means designing and building the interfaces, APIs, and product layer that sit between AI and people. You'll shape how users interact with AI: from chat interfaces and workflows to human-in-the-loop review systems that keep humans in control of agent decisions before they reach customers. Ensuring everything works smoothly, even when the AI doesn't.

You'll own the full stack: frontend experiences that handle streaming responses and unpredictable outputs, backend services that connect AI to core systems, and the pipelines that ship it all into production.

You'll also build the observability and feedback loops that help us continuously improve how these agents perform in production, not just in evaluation, but in the real product.

title: Senior Geotechnical Engineer or Engineering Geologist – Pacific Region
description:
The Senior Geotechnical Engineer or Engineering Geologist – Pacific Region will be focused on supporting GeoEngineers’ strategic expansion into the Indo-Pacific market, particularly Guam. This position is responsible for both technical execution of key activities and project-related deliverables, but also working closely with a market development specialist to identify and advance new business opportunities. Routine responsibilities may include coordination of field exploration programs, construction observation tasks, project management, client-relationship support and development, technical report writing, complex analyses, and development of conceptual models. Essential duties may vary based on project and market demands.


This position will require experience with complex technical challenges, including seismic risk, karst terrain, and deep foundation engineering, specifically relating to waterfront projects across Guam and neighboring island nations. In addition, the position will require conducting construction quality control and special inspection activities to support successful delivery of complex construction projects in the region. This position is a long-term assignment, and will entail close collaboration with our marketing development specialist to build trust and establish and/or strengthen relationships with local firms.


There are two key purposes for this position: 1) bring project management and engineering design expertise to alleviate local firms workload issues, to support business operations and 2) coordinate with our marketing development specialist to seek out and partner with local firms on new project pursuits, in coordination with out federal business development team.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Leads all project management tasks such as developing budgets and scopes, client billings, field report reviews, contract reviews, and proposal development. Partners with Principals and Associates to ensure effective execution of multiple projects.
  • Serves as a technical resource for clients; provides guidance and expertise to solve complex challenges.
  • Coordinates field operations including direction of other field staff as needed. Monitors and guides field staff and subcontractors as required.
  • Oversees detailed explorations and construction activities.
  • Collects field samples as needed (soil, groundwater, surface water, concrete, etc.) in accordance with established protocols.
  • Produces detailed, accurate field notes and prepares field reports in a timely manner.
  • Maintains and operates field equipment/instrumentation in accordance with specified procedures.
  • Develops complete and accurate field reports, figures, tables, etc., that require minimal edits or revisions.
  • Prepares deliverables as required such as field reports, calculations, analyses, etc., and coordinates reviews to ensure high quality and accuracy in accordance with consulting best practices.
  • Leads business-development activities such as identifying potential new clients, attending conferences or professional association meetings, etc.
  • Leads and/or coordinates the development and implementation of field exploration programs and construction projects. Ensures that work performed is consistent with project plans and specifications and in accordance with safety guidelines.
  • Partners with marketing development team to develop compelling relationships for federal pursuits tied to the Indo-Pacific region.
  • Help identify positioning strategies for pursuits in Guam and the Pacific region.
  • Completes engineering analyses and calculations. Develops complex conceptual models (i.e., numerical modeling, hydraulic/hydrologic modeling, etc.)
  • Completes complex spatial analyses (e.g., contours, clipping, buffering).
  • Develops project deliverables related to GIS data such as maps, database organizations, etc.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in the appropriate/assigned field; Master’s degree preferred.
  • 10 years of related professional experience required.
  • Professional Engineer or Certified Engineering Geologist license is required.
  • Advanced-level understanding of related software within discipline such as MathCAD, MODFLOW, FLAC, Civil 3D, Slope/W, LPILE, Settle3, Plaxis, or related software.
  • Ability to consistently meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced work environment.
  • Professional-level verbal and written communication skills.
  • Valid driver’s license.
  • Able to visit and enter military and non-military secure federal installations upon completion of government background checks

Physical Requirements/Work Environment

  • Ability to perform a wide range of physical activities and do heavy work including exerting up to fifty pounds of force on occasion.
  • Able to perform consistent work on a PC.
  • Ability to travel for short-term and long-term assignments as needed. Travel will typically not exceed 40%. Remote field assignments will typically not exceed four weeks in length.
  • All employees are responsible for conducting their work in a safe manner. This includes identifying potential safety hazards and reporting them to the designated project manager in a timely manner and participating in project safety briefings. This also includes wearing appropriate safety equipment when working in the field and completing all required health & safety training prior to beginning field work.

Compensation offered will be based on a variety of individual factors, including education and experience, as well as internal equity. GeoEngineers’ salary ranges are reviewed and updated each year and employees are eligible for pay increases based on individual performance. As part of our competitive total rewards package, employees in this role may also be eligible for our annual year-end bonus offering, subject to program eligibility requirements.


At GeoEngineers, investing in our people is a top priority. In addition to competitive and equitable pay, we are proud to offer a wide range of benefits to support employees and their families, including healthcare (with travel benefit for care not locally available), 401(k) with company match, short-term and long-term disability, life insurance, wellbeing benefits, paid vacation and sick time and paid holidays, among others. View our full listing of benefits here.


Our Commitment to Belonging at GeoEngineers


When people feel they can bring their whole selves to work, that they have a voice and are supported and respected, it creates trust and a feeling of belonging— employees then flourish, grow their careers, and do the best work of their lives. A culture of belonging allows our employees to thrive and our company to prosper. This is a journey, and we are committed to doing the work, learning and evolving as we go.

If you need special assistance or accommodation while seeking employment, please contact Human Resources at hr@geoengineers.com or by phone at (425) 861-6000. We will then make a determination regarding your request for reasonable accommodation on a case-by-case basis.


We welcome and encourage individuals from all backgrounds and experiences to apply for openings on our team. We would love for you to join us!

title: Endpoint Analyst
description:
We are seeking an Endpoint Analyst to independently diagnose and resolve issues related to endpoint connectivity, authentication, and security controls. This role analyzes escalated service desk tickets, leverages logs and security tools to identify root causes, and resolves incidents within defined service level agreements. The analyst applies a consistent, methodical troubleshooting approach while collaborating with IT and security teams.

Responsibilities

  • Analyze and resolve escalated service requests from end users and IT teams
  • Diagnose endpoint issues using user-reported errors, client-side logs, forwarded events, and vendor support tools
  • Troubleshoot network, authentication, and security-related blocks impacting endpoints
  • Develop and maintain knowledge articles to support consistent issue resolution
  • Collaborate with infrastructure, security, and service desk teams to communicate findings and remediation steps
  • Escalate incidents that exceed defined time-to-resolve thresholds

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 3+ years of experience in endpoint support, desktop engineering, or IT/security operations
  • Background in DHCP, DNS, and network access control, along with IP routing and core networking concepts, including packet capture and analysis
  • Knowledge of Active Directory, Windows authentication, and permissions
  • Expertise in troubleshooting HTTP inspection services (e.g., Zscaler), TLS, and PKI issues
  • Skills in using HAR files to diagnose HTTP connection issues from the client side
  • Familiarity with Authenticode signatures and endpoint application control solutions like CyberArk Endpoint Privilege Manager
  • Understanding of endpoint policy mechanisms such as GPO and Intune
  • Proficiency in query tools and log analysis on raw text files and centralized platforms
  • Competency in interpreting common endpoint and security alerts and leveraging online research sources
  • Capability to independently research issues, document clear remediation plans, and apply systematic troubleshooting
  • Clear and professional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a time-sensitive environment
  • Proficiency in English at an Upper-Intermediate level (B2) or higher

Nice to have

  • Relevant technical certifications (e.g., Microsoft, CompTIA, Security-related)
  • Familiarity with authentication protocols such as SAML, Kerberos, and OAuth, as well as OIDC and LDAP
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including Power Query and Pivot Tables
  • Skills in PowerShell scripting for troubleshooting and automation
  • Exposure to endpoint detection and response tools such as Microsoft Defender, Sentinel, or CrowdStrike

description:

  • Join a team making a real impact on biodiversity conservation.

  • Salary range: $65,590 to $76,589 depending on skills and experience.

  • Permanent, full-time position | based in Warkworth.

Our vision: Nature is thriving in Aotearoa | Te Oranga o te Ao Tūroa

Mō te tūranga | About the role

An exciting opportunity has become available for a Biodiversity Ranger within the Tāmaki Makaurau Mainland team. We are looking for a dedicated and collaborative individual to join our team who feels inspired, day in day out, and connected to our united purpose: Toitū te Taiao – We Protect and Restore Nature.

As our next Biodiversity Ranger, you will have the opportunity to work throughout Auckland’s varied and extensive network of public conservation land and coastlines. You’ll be part of our Biodiversity team, working to protect Tāmaki Makaurau’s native species.

The position will be focussed on:

  • Leading the response to wildlife incidents across the district,

  • Handling public enquiries related to native wildlife,

  • Carrying out public education, advocacy and light compliance work around local wildlife

  • Working with stakeholders including iwi, hapū and whānau,

  • Facilitating research and record-keeping

  • Working on other Biodiversity conservation projects throughout the region as required.

We’re looking for someone who can handle it all – from our smallest native Manu (birds) to giant tohorā (whales).

Click here for the Role Description

Ngā pūkenga me ngā wheako | Skills and experience

If you have some of following, we are keen to hear from you:

  • A tertiary qualification related to conservation management, ecology, or natural sciences, or 2+ years’ equivalent practical experience working in any related area.

  • Familiarity with native wildlife and skills in how to handle them.

  • A track record of excellent relationship management, especially with communities, volunteers, statutory bodies, iwi, hapū and whānau.

  • Experience in a public-facing role or handling public enquiries, either in-person or remotely, such as in a customer-service or public advocacy capacity.

  • Ability to communicate professionally and clearly with a range of audiences in-person and via phone and email.

  • Ability and self-motivation to work independently in the outdoors.

  • Familiarity using a range of office software including Word, Excel, MS Teams, Outlook etc.

  • Reasonable physical fitness and mobility.

  • Full clean driving licence, including the ability to drive a manual vehicle.

  • Availability for occasional evening and weekend work.

Desirable:

  • Familiar with local and national conservation legislation.

  • Working knowledge of iwi landscape in Tāmaki Makaurau.

  • Familiarity with how concepts in te ao Māori such as Kaitiakitanga and mātauranga Māori influence conservation management.

  • Familiarity with how Te Tiriti o Waitangi / the Treaty of Waitangi is upheld through work in the public service, and a general commitment to upholding the values of Te Tiriti/ the Treaty.

  • Experience in, or knowledge of, safe handling techniques for wildlife such as birds, lizards, or seals.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
About Nevis

Nevis is building the world’s first AI wealth management platform. In just 9 months, Nevis has grown to have over $50 billion of assets under management on its platform and is on track to have over $100 billion by the end of this year.

Nevis is also backed by world leading investors and has raised a total of $40 million from Sequoia Capital, ICONIQ and Ribbit. Together it makes Nevis one of the highest funded and fastest growing Series A startups in Europe.

The Role

We are looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to be the technical counterpart for our customers and make sure every implementation succeeds.

When one of the largest wealth management firms in the country decides to run on Nevis, you are the engineer in the room with them. You learn how their business actually works, translate that into what we build and configure, and own the technical side of the deployment from first workshop to a platform their advisors use every day. You work with their engineers, their operations team and their vendors, and you stay their technical point of contact long after go-live.

The work spans whatever the deployment needs: integrations with the systems they already run, getting their data into our platform, configuring and deploying AI agents and workflows against their real processes, prototyping fast to show what is possible, and being the person who diagnoses it when something does not behave the way anyone expected.

You will be trusted by the customer and relied on internally, so two things have to be true at once. You have to be precise, because these firms make decisions on the numbers we show them. And you have to move fast with whatever tools get you there, because the problems are novel and nobody is handing you a specification

What You’ll Do

  • Own the technical side of enterprise deployments end to end, from initial scoping through go-live and expansion

  • Be the customer's main technical point of contact, working alongside their engineers, operations teams and leadership

  • Understand how each firm operates deeply enough to translate their workflows into what Nevis builds, configures and automates for them

  • Design and deliver the integrations and data flows a deployment depends on, working with our engineering teams to make the pipes right

  • Configure and deploy AI agents and automated workflows against real customer processes, and tune them until they hold up in production

  • Build prototypes and demos fast, so customers can see what is possible before anyone commits to building it

  • Diagnose and resolve technical issues in live deployments, and be honest with customers about what the platform can and cannot do

  • Partner with Deployment Strategists on the commercial relationship, giving them the technical grounding that wins and grows accounts

  • Feed what you learn in the field back into the product, shaping the roadmap so every future customer inherits it

Who You Are

  • You have 3+ years in a forward deployed, solutions engineering, technical implementation or similar customer-facing engineering role at a high-growth technology company

  • You are a strong engineer. Python and SQL are second nature, and you are comfortable working across systems, APIs and messy real-world data

  • You have put LLMs and agentic tooling into production, and you have judgment about where they are reliable and where they are not

  • You build fast. You would rather ship something working and iterate than design something perfect on paper

  • You are precise about numbers. You know the difference between an honest "the data cannot answer that" and a confident wrong answer, and you know which one costs more

  • You communicate exceptionally well with people who are not engineers. You can walk a COO through what you built and where it is weak without losing them

  • You have low ego and high ownership. You do what needs to be done and the outcome matters more than the credit

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity, and you bring clarity to unstructured problems rather than frustration

  • You are happy to travel and work onsite with customers

  • STEM degree from a top university, or equivalent demonstrated experience

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience in wealth management, financial services or fintec

  • Familiarity with the US RIA landscape, including how large advisory firms are structured, regulated and operated

  • Experience with data integration, pipelines or systems migration at enterprise scale

  • You are at the frontier of using LLM-powered workflows in your day-to-day work, with hands-on fluency across tools like Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or similar

Why Join Nevis?

  • Work alongside a high-calibre founding team backed by some of the best investors in the world

  • A fast-paced, high-growth environment with the opportunity to shape how the business operates

  • Be part of a mission-driven company transforming the wealth management industry with huge potential for global impact

  • 25 days’ annual leave & Bank Holidays

  • Private medical insurance

  • Competitive salary and benefits package, including company equity
