title: Salesforce Lead
description:
Eightcap operates at the intersection of cutting-edge technology and global financial markets. Headquartered in Melbourne with a global footprint spanning the UK, Cyprus, and Bulgaria, we build the high-performance infrastructure that connects the world to CFD markets - reliably, securely and with precision.

Eightcap is looking for a Salesforce Lead to own our Salesforce platform end to end. This is a hands-on role, roughly 70% building, configuring and developing, 30% leading a small team and shaping where the platform goes next.

You'll sit at the centre of the business. Sales, Customer Service, Marketing, Legal & Compliance and Finance all run on Salesforce, and you'll be the person they come to when they need something built, fixed, automated or rethought. That means translating business problems into clean platform solutions, debating when a request isn't the right answer, and keeping the organisation from turning into technical debt.

We're also investing in Salesforce Voice / Service Cloud Voice as the backbone of our contact centre, so there's real greenfield work alongside the day-to-day. Aligning this to our Agentforce work is one of the top priorities.

As the Salesforce Lead, you will:

  • Own the Salesforce roadmap alongside the CTO: prioritise, sequence and communicate what's coming and why.
  • Lead, mentor and grow a team of 2–3 admins/developers; set standards for release management, documentation and code quality.
  • Build it yourself: declarative configuration, Flow, Apex, LWC, integrations and data modelling.
  • Partner with Sales, Service, Marketing, Legal & Compliance and Finance to gather requirements and deliver solutions that actually get adopted.
  • Design, deploy and optimise Service Cloud Voice / Salesforce Voice for our contact centre — routing, telephony integration, agent experience, call analytics.
  • Keep the platform compliant and audit-ready: permissions, data access, retention, and controls that satisfy Legal & Compliance in a regulated financial services environment.
  • Manage the release cycle, sandbox strategy and third-party AppExchange/vendor relationships.
  • Monitor org health, technical debt and licence utilisation, and make the case for change when it's needed.

Requirements

Essential:

  • 5+ years working on Salesforce, including significant time as a senior administrator or technical lead.
  • Strong Apex, SOQL and Flow skills — you can build, review and debug production code.
  • Deep administration capability: security model, sharing, data management, deployment tooling.
  • Experience leading or mentoring other Salesforce professionals.
  • Track record working directly with multiple business functions and translating their needs into a coherent platform, not a pile of one-off requests.
  • Salesforce Voice / Service Cloud Voice or contact centre platform experience (CTI, omni-channel routing, telephony integration).
  • Comfortable planning: roadmaps, estimates, trade-offs, and explaining technical decisions to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Salesforce Administrator and Platform Developer I Certifications.

Nice to have:

  • Financial services, fintech, trading or other regulated industry background.
  • Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing (Cloud and/or thirdparty) and Experience Cloud exposure.
  • CI/CD for Salesforce (Gearset).
  • Advanced Administrator, Platform Developer II, or Application/System Architect certifications.
  • Integration experience with middleware, APIs or data platforms.

Benefits

What's it like to work at Eightcap?

We have built a performance-driven environment where you're given the autonomy to drive change and the accountability to own the results. We provide a space for the ambitious, adaptable and collaborative to deliver outcomes that fuel our success while building the skills and experience that defines a career.

We also support you through:

  • Ongoing investment in your career development, including technical and professional training.
  • Wellness and lifestyle perks, such as monthly corporate massages.
  • Drinks every Friday at 4pm.
  • Parental leave entitlements.
  • Staff referral bonus programme.
  • Annual flu vaccinations.
  • Purchased leave.
  • Novated leasing options for vehicle financing and management.
  • A great CBD location with easy access to public transport.
  • A multicultural, collaborative and supportive team culture.
  • Being part of exciting new projects for the company.
  • Regular social activities.

title: EAP Counsellor
description:
Who we are:

At Workplace Options (WPO), we deliver human-centric solutions that empower people to thrive personally and professionally. With a global team of more than 4,800 professionals, we provide real-time emotional support, therapy, coaching, mindfulness, and family services to millions worldwide. Since 1982, we’ve partnered with employers, health plans, and insurers to design flexible, forward-thinking programs that evolve alongside today’s changing workforce.

Today, we support 160 million people across 150,000 organizations, including over half of Fortune 500 companies. Now part of the TELUS Health family, we are expanding our global impact by combining decades of wellbeing expertise. Together, we’re building healthier, more resilient organizations—one person at a time.

Current Opportunity: EAP Counsellor

Location: Ireland
Full-time/Part-time: Full-time (40 hours per week)
Salary: €35,200 - €38,720 plus competitive benefits offering
Onsite/Hybrid/Remote: Hybrid or remote depending on your location

What you will do:

Our EAP Counsellors engage with participants over the phone, video, chat & email all while demonstrating what we call: The Power of a Good Conversation – creating a connection with the client to ensure they feel heard, supported, and cared for.

It’s difficult to define an “average day” for our counsellors, as every caller brings a unique set of experiences and challenges. Through thoughtful clinical conversations, our counsellors support each individual in exploring their situation and finding a path forward. These short videos provide a good insight into what it’s like to be a counsellor here at Workplace Options: Being a Counsellor at WPO and Member Experience - The Power of a Good Conversation

If you are a mental health provider that wants to provide emotional support with a warm and empathic approach to people of all ages, cultures, and backgrounds from around the world, this is the role for you.

Responsibilities:
  • Provide single session telephonic and video counselling, in-the-moment support and crisis telephonic management in a supportive, ethical and professional manner while maintaining client-confidentiality.
  • Assess clients thoroughly to ensure appropriateness for short-term counselling.
  • Assess and manage high risk calls and working closely with individuals at risk.
  • Appropriately refer clients to external resources or within WPO as part of our holistic approach.
  • Maintain clear clinical and task-oriented documentation in case management system.
  • Deliver comprehensive administrative support, acting as a key point of contact to assist clients and providers with service-related enquiries and issue resolution.
  • Any additional tasks pertinent to the position, as deemed appropriate by management.

Qualifications/Skills:

To excel in this role, you will need the following qualifications and skills:
  • Minimum of a Level 4 diploma in Counselling.
  • Membership of a regulatory counselling body (IACP/Other) and either full accreditation or working towards accreditation.
  • Experience using short-term counselling modalities such as Solution-Focused, CBT, Mindfulness, Integrative, Systemic counselling.
  • Training in crisis intervention and supporting high risk clients beneficial.
  • Passionate about providing support to clients from anywhere in the world.
  • Culturally sensitive to our clients and flexible using a telephonic interpreter as needed.
  • Competent in using our various methods of contact – telephone, video, email, text and live chat.
  • Ability to work with clients presenting with substance abuse, situations of crisis, mental health symptoms and/or family/relationship-related concerns impacting personal or work performance.

What we offer:

At Workplace Options, we don’t just deliver wellbeing services to our clients, we champion wellbeing for our own employees as well. Examples of our benefits and commitment to employee wellbeing include:

Gym reimbursement, Tuition reimbursement, Life insurance, Employers pension contribution, Clinical supervision, Supervision stipend for those working towards accreditation, 24/7 support for risk calls, Mentorship programme, CPD training reimbursement, Access to professional monthly clinical development webinars & professional development workshops, Accrediting body membership reimbursement, EAP benefits, Employee exchange programme.


At Workplace Options, we are committed to and are accountable for building a workplace where individuals feel empowered to bring their whole selves to work, free from judgment or fear of discrimination. We understand that having a diverse organization is only the beginning and it will require nurturing and care to thrive. We will continue to take action to ensure we achieve equitable and measurable outcomes.

We strive to cultivate a space where diverse voices are not only heard but actively sought out and valued for the unique insights they bring. By embracing and promoting authenticity, we aim to build a vibrant and inclusive community that fosters collaboration, innovation, belonging and personal growth.

For further details about WPO please check out our website and these short videos give a great overview of what we do Human-Powered Care and The WPO Global Experience
